WASM-002 Canonical Run Receipts

A saved immutable WKO is the durable record of analyst authorization. A Receipt is the durable record of the governed execution attempt. WASM-002 therefore creates a small deterministic TXT sidecar after every actual Run invocation of a saved WKO, whether the run succeeds or refuses. Receipt generation is engine infrastructure and is never a Work Order instruction.

W002-RCP-001

Every actual Run invocation of a saved WKO automatically produces one Receipt attempt

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

When the analyst invokes Run on a saved immutable WKO, Data Sculptor must automatically create one governed run-receipt attempt for that invocation. The Work Order must not require a RECEIPT, SAVE RECEIPT, or equivalent clause.

An editable unsaved WIP is non-executable under the Work Order lifecycle contract and therefore cannot produce an execution Receipt. A saved WKO that is invoked and then refuses during validation or execution still has an execution outcome and must receive a refusal Receipt when receipt publication succeeds.

W002-RCP-002

The canonical WASM-002 Receipt is a governed TXT artifact with its own creation timestamp

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The physical Receipt filename is:

__DS__RCP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.txt

The UTC token belongs to the Receipt artifact itself and represents the Receipt's governed creation/publication time under the canonical artifact-identity rules. It must not be copied from the authorizing WKO's filename merely to make the two filenames share a timestamp.

The file is written visibly in the flat Suitcase under the governed RCP artifact class. Data Sculptor chooses the governed filename; the analyst does not supply it.

W002-RCP-003

WASM-002 Receipts are TXT-only and independent of presentation state

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

For WASM-002, the canonical run Receipt is always plain TXT. Browser theme, built-in HTML presentation, Help voice, or other presentation state must not change whether the run Receipt is emitted as TXT or alter its governed facts.

WASM-002 must not emit an HTML Receipt as an alternative to the canonical TXT Receipt. Configurable Brand Manifest behavior is deferred to a future build.

W002-RCP-004

Future branded HTML Receipts must render the same canonical receipt facts

DEFERRED
SCOPEV1-BACKLOGBUILD—

A later product revision may permit a valid governed branding definition, including a future TOML serialization if adopted, to render the canonical Receipt facts as branded self-contained HTML. Such rendering is presentation only.

The HTML representation must not change, omit, reinterpret, weaken, or invent analytical facts relative to the canonical receipt-fact model. The exact future switch between TXT and branded HTML, whether both are retained, the TOML/Brand Manifest serialization, and HTML rendering details are outside the WASM-002 freeze.

W002-RCP-005

Canonical Receipt TXT serialization is deterministic

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The WASM-002 Receipt is UTF-8 without BOM and uses LF (0x0A) line endings. Every Receipt ends with exactly one final LF. No serialized line carries trailing spaces, and no blank physical lines are emitted unless a later operation-specific grammar explicitly freezes them.

It is a deterministic line-oriented KEY: VALUE document with a frozen core-key order followed by operation-specific fact sections in deterministic order. KEY is an uppercase ASCII field name. The separator is exactly one ASCII colon followed by exactly one ASCII space. KEY=VALUE is not valid canonical Receipt serialization.

Fixed machine tokens and non-negative decimal integers are serialized unquoted. Human-authored text, filenames, aliases, headers, and other free text are serialized as double-quoted UTF-8 strings. Inside a quoted value, a literal double quote is represented by doubling it as "". CR and LF are not permitted inside a single serialized value; each fact remains exactly one physical line.

Enumerated values use the exact uppercase tokens frozen by the applicable requirement. Non-negative integers use ungrouped ASCII base-10 digits. This shared text rule is normative for all Receipt free-text values and is acceptance-tested byte-for-byte.

W002-RCP-006

Every Receipt records the fixed core execution facts and exact WKO lineage

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Every canonical WASM-002 Receipt begins with the following common envelope keys in exactly this order:

  1. RECEIPT_VERSION
  2. RECEIPT_FILENAME
  3. RECEIPT_UTC
  4. WORK_ORDER_FILENAME
  5. OPERATION
  6. RUN_STARTED_UTC
  7. RUN_FINISHED_UTC
  8. RESULT
  9. DIAGNOSTIC_ID
  10. IDENTITY_COLLISION_RETRIES

Day 060 H-02 version freeze: RECEIPT_VERSION is the unquoted integer 1 for the WASM-002 Receipt contract.

RECEIPT_FILENAME is the exact physical governed RCP filename. RECEIPT_UTC is exactly the canonical UTC timestamp embedded in that filename and is distinct from the run start/finish timestamps. WORK_ORDER_FILENAME is the exact physical immutable WKO identity invoked and is the authoritative WKO→RCP lineage link.

Day 060 H-09 / BM-06 truthful run-timestamp semantics

RUN_STARTED_UTC and RUN_FINISHED_UTC are governed truthful host-UTC observations at millisecond precision. They are not decorative labels and are not synthesized from artifact filenames.

  • RUN_STARTED_UTC is observed only after the exact saved WKO has been resolved and found eligible to Run, and immediately before operation-specific validation/execution begins. It therefore brackets operation validation, analytical work, publication attempts, refusal processing, and any governed rollback/cleanup performed by that Run.
  • RUN_FINISHED_UTC is observed only after the operation has reached its final SUCCESS or REFUSED analytical outcome and all non-Receipt governed effects are settled: successful artifacts are committed, refusal state is established, and required rollback/cleanup or retained non-authoritative evidence classification is complete. Receipt publication begins only after this observation.

For one Run, the truthful temporal invariant is:

WKO_UTC ≤ RUN_STARTED_UTC ≤ each successfully published run-artifact UTC ≤ RUN_FINISHED_UTC ≤ RECEIPT_UTC

where WKO_UTC is the governed UTC token embedded in the exact WORK_ORDER_FILENAME, and “run-artifact UTC” means the governed UTC embedded in each non-Receipt artifact successfully published by that Run, including a shared materialization transaction UTC where applicable. An operation that publishes no non-Receipt artifact simply has no middle artifact-UTC comparison.

Equality is permitted because the canonical timestamp precision is milliseconds. Data Sculptor must not fabricate, increment, decrement, or reorder UTC values merely to make this invariant appear true. Receipt fixtures and retained acceptance evidence must use physically possible timelines under this rule.

The existing rule that WKO and Receipt filename timestamps are not required to match remains unchanged: they are distinct events, but a WKO invoked by a Run must already exist as a governed artifact before that Run begins.

RESULT is a closed WASM-002 vocabulary containing exactly SUCCESS and REFUSED. No other RESULT token is valid. DIAGNOSTIC_ID: NONE is used for an ordinary successful run; a refused run carries the exact governed diagnostic identity.

The shared governed absence-state vocabulary is closed to these four tokens, with these exact meanings:

  • NONE — the fact is applicable and definitively has no value in this event;
  • NOT_RUN — the owning stage or operation was not executed;
  • NOT_AVAILABLE — the fact is applicable or potentially applicable, but its value could not be obtained;
  • NOT_APPLICABLE — the fact does not apply to this event, diagnostic, operation, or artifact.

These states are semantically distinct and must not be substituted for one another. A count that was actually established as zero is serialized as the integer 0, never as an absence token.

The refusal-serialization matrix for every present operation-specific key is deterministic:

State of the key's owning fact/stage at refusalRequired serialization
The fact was authoritatively established before refusalSerialize the exact governed value.
The owning stage was never enteredNOT_RUN.
The owning stage ran and definitively produced no value/artifact for this eventNONE.
The fact applies but could not be obtainedNOT_AVAILABLE.
The fact does not apply to this eventNOT_APPLICABLE.
An applicable count was authoritatively established as zero0.
A publication identity whose publication stage was never enteredNOT_RUN, except where an earlier frozen operation-specific rule explicitly fixes another token.
A publication identity whose publication stage was entered but no artifact of that identity successfully publishedNONE.
A publication identity that successfully publishedThe exact physical governed filename.

For this contract, a fact is established only when its owning validation/stage has deterministically fixed the value and later execution cannot revise that fact. Candidate allocation, partial bytes, or an uncommitted publication does not establish a published-artifact identity.

If parsing/validation refuses before one of the seven governed WASM-002 operations can be identified, the Receipt uses OPERATION: UNKNOWN_OPERATION, RESULT: REFUSED, and the applicable DIAGNOSTIC_ID. After the common envelope there is no operation-specific section; the Receipt proceeds directly to CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT: 0. UNKNOWN_OPERATION is not an executable operation.

After all operation-specific facts and indexed lists, every Receipt ends with:

CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT: <N>
CREATED_ARTIFACT_001: "..."
...
CREATED_ARTIFACT_N: "..."

The created-artifact list contains only exact physical governed filenames successfully published by the run, excluding the Receipt itself. For this accounting, an artifact is successfully published only if it remains a committed governed artifact when the Run finishes; an artifact promoted and then rolled back, or left only as non-authoritative failure residue under All-or-Refuse, is excluded from CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT and its indexed list. Indexed suffixes are one-based decimal with a minimum width of three digits and no maximum width: 001 through 999 are zero-padded and 1000 onward uses the ordinary full ungrouped decimal form. When a count is zero, no indexed lines for that list appear.

IDENTITY_COLLISION_RETRIES is always present and is 0 when no governed filename-allocation retry occurred. Receipt/WKO filename timestamps are not required to match. One immutable WKO may be run multiple times, each producing a distinct Receipt that points back to the same exact WORK_ORDER_FILENAME.

F-08 DS-STEPS / Receipt token separation. Human-authored Work Orders use the readable terminal clauses below; the Receipt serializes the corresponding machine token in OPERATION. The two columns are not interchangeable spellings:

DS-STEPS terminal clauseReceipt OPERATION
MATERIALIZEMATERIALIZE
INVENTORYINVENTORY
UPDATE ALIASESUPDATE_ALIASES
REPAIR MAPREPAIR_MAP
REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRYREPAIR_WORK_ORDER_REGISTRY
CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8CONVERT_WINDOWS_1252_TO_UTF_8
CATALOG STORESCATALOG_STORES

For example, REPAIR_MAP is not valid DS-STEPS syntax and REPAIR MAP is not the serialized Receipt token. UNKNOWN_OPERATION remains a refusal-only Receipt value when validation cannot identify one of these seven operations; it is not an executable operation.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

For a WASM-002 MATERIALIZE run, after the common envelope the Receipt serializes these operation-specific keys in exactly this order:

  1. SOURCE_FILENAME
  2. BASE_MAP_FILENAME

BASE_MAP_FILENAME: NONE denotes a newly established Store with no predecessor Store MAP.

Day 060 H-11 / BM-08 RID_ACTION ownership and establishment

RID_ACTION is a governed execution fact describing what this Run actually established for the Store RID path. It is never an intention, plan, or prediction.

  • RID_ACTION: REUSED is established when routing has selected an existing Store, the exact inherited RID filename is known, and that inherited RID has passed the validation required to proceed. Because the RID already exists, this fact may be established before Stage 1 or Stage 2 completes.
  • RID_ACTION: CREATED is established only when a new-Store RID candidate has successfully completed governed promotion into its final RID identity. Merely planning, allocating, writing, closing, validating, or naming an SCR candidate does not establish CREATED.
  • Until either of those facts is established, the common refusal matrix governs RID_ACTION. For a new-Store path that refuses before successful RID promotion, RID_ACTION is NOT_RUN. If an existing-Store route is identified but the required inherited RID fact cannot be validly established, RID_ACTION is NOT_AVAILABLE.

RID_FILENAME is a separate fact:

  • for REUSED, it is the exact already-published inherited RID filename as soon as reuse is established;
  • for CREATED, it is the exact governed final RID filename only after successful RID promotion;
  • before new-RID promotion succeeds, no candidate/SCR filename may be serialized as though it were a published RID.

With RID_ACTION: CREATED, RID_FILENAME records the RID identity successfully promoted during the Run even if that RID is later rolled back under All-or-Refuse; rollback does not erase the already-established RID_ACTION/RID_FILENAME execution facts.

The refusal-boundary matrix is therefore:

Materialization stateRID_ACTIONRID_FILENAME
Validation/routing refuses before a Store/RID path is establishedNOT_RUNNOT_RUN or NOT_AVAILABLE only when an applicable routing fact could not be obtained under the common matrix
New Store; Stage 1 refusalNOT_RUNNOT_RUN
New Store; Stage 2 refusalNOT_RUNNOT_RUN
New Store; post-Stage-2 gate refusal before RID promotionNOT_RUNNOT_RUN
New Store; RID candidate/promotion has not successfully completedNOT_RUNNOT_RUN
New Store; RID promotion succeedsCREATEDexact published RID filename
Existing Store; exact inherited RID selected and validatedREUSEDexact inherited RID filename
Existing Store; later Stage 1, Stage 2, gate, or publication refusal after reuse was establishedREUSEDexact inherited RID filename
Existing lineage identified but required inherited RID cannot be validly establishedNOT_AVAILABLENOT_AVAILABLE

A refusal Receipt that says RID_ACTION: CREATED while RID_FILENAME is NONE or NOT_RUN and no RID was successfully promoted is invalid evidence.

STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME has exactly two completed Stage-1 values: PASS and FAIL. If Stage 1 never ran, the value is NOT_RUN. If Stage 1 began but a separate failure prevented a governed PASS/FAIL determination, the value is NOT_AVAILABLE. NOT_APPLICABLE is not valid for this key.

UTF8_FIRST_INVALID_BYTE_OFFSET and UTF8_STOP_REASON are refusal-only Stage-1 evidence. On STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME: FAIL, the offset is mandatory and is the exact zero-based absolute physical source-byte offset of the first byte of the invalid sequence, and the stop reason is mandatory and exactly INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE. Neither field may be NOT_AVAILABLE when the Stage-1 outcome is FAIL. On PASS, both fields are NOT_APPLICABLE. If Stage 1 never ran, both are NOT_RUN. If Stage 1 began but no UTF-8 PASS/FAIL conclusion was established because of a separate failure, both refusal-only fields are NOT_APPLICABLE.

WINDOWS_1252_COMPATIBILITY_OUTCOME and WINDOWS_1252_FIRST_UNDEFINED_BYTE_OFFSET are the governed F-16 follow-on facts. They are evaluated only after STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME: FAIL. When the complete second pass reaches EOF with every byte mappable, the outcome is COMPATIBLE and the offset is NOT_APPLICABLE. When the pass encounters one of the undefined bytes frozen in W002-CONV-002.4, the outcome is INCOMPATIBLE and the offset is the exact zero-based absolute physical source-byte offset of the first such byte. If the pass begins but an independent failure prevents a conclusion, both fields are NOT_AVAILABLE. If Stage 1 did not conclude FAIL, the compatibility pass does not run and both fields are NOT_RUN.

The five exact CSV refusal keys CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION, CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET, CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE, CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD, and CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL carry the exact structural CSV refusal condition and location oracle frozen in W002-MAT-002.8. If Stage 2 never ran, all five are NOT_RUN; if Stage 2 completed without an applicable CSV refusal, all five are NOT_APPLICABLE; on a CSV refusal, each established location fact is serialized and any applicable fact that could not be obtained is NOT_AVAILABLE.

The MATERIALIZE refusal-stage matrix is:

Any RID fact already established before this later refusal remains governed by the RID_ACTION/RID_FILENAME matrix above. Day 060 H-24 / BM-08 publication-boundary split: these two MATERIALIZE publication-refusal rows apply the common W002-RCP-006 ownership rule to the successor-MAP publication stage. NOT_RUN means that stage was never entered; NONE means it was entered but no successor MAP successfully published. The early boundary is exercised by the RID identity-allocation exhaustion fixture; the later boundary has its own byte-exact golden fixture.

OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_COUNT is NOT_RUN until operational-name resolution has run; afterward it is the established non-negative count, including literal 0. Fallback records are ordered by ascending physical source-column ordinal. the exact fallback key OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_<INDEX>_REASON is exactly SOURCE_HEADER_EXCEEDS_1024_SCALARS.

For successful Store-establishing materialization, the common created-artifact list is ordered RID first, newly published COLs in resolved KEEP order, then successor MAP. For successful existing-Store materialization, the inherited RID is not newly created; the list contains newly published COLs in resolved KEEP order followed by the successor MAP.

P3-09 Receipt oracle: when Stage 2 refuses because the certified source contains no logical CSV record, the five CSV refusal fields must serialize exactly as CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION: NO_HEADER_RECORD, CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET: <exact source byte length>, CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE: 1, CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD: 1, and CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL: 1.

Day 060 H-13 / BM-10 clarification: within those five governed CSV refusal fields, the zero-byte and UTF-8-BOM-only cases differ only in CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET: 0 versus 3. Their complete Receipt bytes also differ wherever the underlying source identity, certified source byte count, Work Order identity, run/Receipt timestamps, Receipt filename/UUID, or other fixture-specific governed facts differ. The complete Receipts must never be described as differing only by one field.

F-20 operational-name Receipt oracle: OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_COUNT counts selected/materialized columns whose exact source header exceeded 1,024 Unicode scalar values. Each corresponding ..._ASSIGNED_NAME stores the final deterministic operational/default-alias name after any permitted fallback collision disambiguation; ..._REASON remains exactly SOURCE_HEADER_EXCEEDS_1024_SCALARS. The Receipt does not copy the oversized exact source header merely to explain the fallback.

The common indexed-key rule from W002-RCP-006 applies without a maximum width. A full-width KEEP is therefore representable through PUBLISHED_COL_16384_FILENAME (and corresponding fallback indexes when applicable); the three-digit examples are a minimum-width convention, not a 999-item ceiling.

Day 060 H-10 / BM-07 count semantics: REGISTERED_CURRENT_COUNT and REGISTERED_DEPRECATED_COUNT count only previously unregistered structurally valid WKOs that this repair Run newly adds to the successor WKO MAP with the stated status. They do not count surviving pre-existing rows already present in the base registry. The indexed filename lines list exactly the corresponding newly registered WKOs and no others.

If the bootstrap repair WKO is one of those newly registered WKOs, it must appear in exactly one registered list. A successful repair Receipt that omits a newly registered bootstrap repair WKO is invalid evidence.

CONVERT_WINDOWS_1252_TO_UTF_8

  1. SOURCE_FILENAME
  2. SOURCE_ENCODING
  3. UNDEFINED_WINDOWS_1252_BYTE_OFFSET
  4. MATERIALIZED_ENCODING
  5. TRANSCODING
  6. SOURCE_CHANGED
  7. OUTPUT_FILENAME

UNDEFINED_WINDOWS_1252_BYTE_OFFSET is the zero-based absolute physical source-byte offset of the first byte undefined by the frozen Windows-1252 mapping when that refusal occurs. If the compatibility stage never ran it is NOT_RUN; if the stage ran and no undefined-byte refusal occurred it is NOT_APPLICABLE; if the fact applies but could not be obtained it is NOT_AVAILABLE.

Day 060 H-14 / BM-11 undefined-Windows-1252-byte refusal oracle

For CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8, an undefined Windows-1252 byte is detected during the complete pre-transcoding compatibility assessment. Transcoding has not begun when this refusal is established.

When the complete compatibility assessment encounters the first undefined byte, the Receipt must serialize these exact operation facts:

SOURCE_ENCODING: WINDOWS-1252-INCOMPATIBLE
UNDEFINED_WINDOWS_1252_BYTE_OFFSET: <exact zero-based absolute physical source-byte offset>
MATERIALIZED_ENCODING: NOT_RUN
TRANSCODING: NOT_RUN
SOURCE_CHANGED: NO
OUTPUT_FILENAME: NONE

WINDOWS-1252-INCOMPATIBLE is the exact SOURCE_ENCODING token for this governed CONVERT refusal. OUTPUT_FILENAME: NONE means the operation definitively established that no CVT was published for the event. No CVT candidate may be reported as output.

The compatibility scan reports the first undefined byte only. Later undefined bytes do not replace that offset. Permitted changes in scan buffer/window size or boundary placement must not change the reported absolute offset.

Day 060 H-25 / BM-04 already-valid-UTF-8 refusal oracle. If the complete bound source passes strict UTF-8 validation, CONVERT refuses as unnecessary before Windows-1252 compatibility assessment or transcoding. The Receipt must serialize these exact operation facts:

SOURCE_ENCODING: UTF-8
UNDEFINED_WINDOWS_1252_BYTE_OFFSET: NOT_RUN
MATERIALIZED_ENCODING: NOT_RUN
TRANSCODING: NOT_RUN
SOURCE_CHANGED: NO
OUTPUT_FILENAME: NONE

UTF-8 is the exact SOURCE_ENCODING token for this governed refusal. OUTPUT_FILENAME: NONE means the classification gate definitively established that this event publishes no CVT. The Windows-1252 compatibility stage is not entered.

W002-RCP-009

Receipt truth is execution evidence, not presentation authority

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The Receipt records what Data Sculptor actually attempted, observed, refused, and successfully published. It must not reinterpret the analyst's WKO, replace the Store MAP, or become a second analytical command surface.

The WKO remains the durable authorization record; Store MAP/RID/COL artifacts remain the governed analytical state; diagnostic events remain the refusal/help truth; the Receipt cross-references those facts as the durable run ledger. The body of published canonical RCP artifacts is the authoritative evidence substrate for the Flight Recorder logical view defined in W002-STOR-012.

W002-RCP-010

Receipt-publication failure is itself a governed evidence failure

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Data Sculptor must never claim that a durable Receipt exists until the RCP file has been successfully written and closed in the Suitcase. If host or filesystem failure prevents Receipt publication, the browser must surface a canonical diagnostic through the Help Engine stating that receipt evidence could not be persisted.

A receipt-publication failure does not retroactively falsify analytical artifacts that were already successfully committed under their own publication contracts, but the user-facing run summary must clearly distinguish analytical outcome from receipt-persistence failure. Data Sculptor must not invent, backdate, or silently reconstruct a Receipt and present it as the original run artifact.

F-14 publication path, reconciled by F-33: the RCP itself is first written as the corresponding SCR candidate under W002-STOR-023.1, closed, reopened and validated against the exact Receipt serialization/key contract before the class-token rename to RCP. If final RCP promotion fails, the candidate remains non-authoritative SCR evidence. Help may identify the exact retained SCR filename when that fact was established, but it must still state that the canonical Receipt was not persisted. WASM-002 does not emit an RCV artifact for this failure.

W002-RCP-011

Future RID recovery Receipt contract is deferred

DEFERRED
SCOPEV1-BACKLOGBUILD—

RECOVER_RID is not a valid WASM-002 Receipt OPERATION token. No WASM-002 Receipt key table for RID recovery is defined.

If a later V1 revision introduces governed RID recovery, its Receipt operation token, exact key order, refusal matrix, publication identities, provenance, and golden-byte fixtures must be frozen explicitly before implementation. This deferred requirement preserves the evidence intent without creating a current executable surface.

W002-RCP-ACC-001

Successful materialization Receipt and WKO-lineage acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A Store-establishing materialization fixture must run one saved WKO, publish exactly one canonical TXT RCP, and prove that the Receipt identifies the exact WKO through WORK_ORDER_FILENAME, source, RID_ACTION: CREATED, new RID, Stage 1 result/bytes/time, Stage 2 row count/time, all requested COL artifacts in resolved KEEP order, successor Store MAP, published-artifact count, timestamps, and RESULT: SUCCESS. The RCP filename UTC must represent the Receipt artifact's own creation/publication event and must not be required to equal the WKO filename UTC.

The same immutable WKO must then be executable again in an appropriate fixture, producing a second distinct RCP with its own Receipt/run timestamps while both Receipts contain the same exact WORK_ORDER_FILENAME. A later same-Store materialization fixture must additionally prove RID_ACTION: REUSED and the original RID filename.

The Store-establishing fixture must also prove that the newly created RID, every newly created COL, and the successor MAP carry one identical publication-transaction UTC token while each has a distinct UUID; the RCP filename UTC remains its own Receipt publication timestamp and is not required to equal that analytical transaction UTC. A later same-Store materialization must prove that newly created COLs and its successor MAP share the later transaction UTC while the inherited RID retains its original timestamp/UUID.

F-07 Stage-1 success fixture: a successful materialization Receipt must serialize STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME: PASS, with UTF8_FIRST_INVALID_BYTE_OFFSET: NOT_APPLICABLE and UTF8_STOP_REASON: NOT_APPLICABLE. Separate refusal fixtures under W002-RCP-ACC-002 must prove FAIL plus the mandatory exact offset and INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE.

F-20 maximum-width Receipt acceptance: a successful full-width materialization fixture must prove that published-COL indexed keys continue through PUBLISHED_COL_16384_FILENAME using the minimum-three-digit/no-maximum suffix rule. Oversized-header fixtures must prove the exact fallback count, source ordinal, assigned operational name, and SOURCE_HEADER_EXCEEDS_1024_SCALARS reason without embedding the oversized source-header text in the Receipt merely as fallback evidence.

F-23 additional successful-Receipt coverage: acceptance must include a successful INVENTORY run whose RCP carries the exact governed INVENTORY operation-specific facts and a successful UPDATE_ALIASES run whose RCP carries the exact BASE_MAP_FILENAME and SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME while reporting only actually published artifacts in the common created-artifact tail.

F-23 UUID-collision seam: using a controlled UUID sequence, acceptance must force one or more governed filename collisions before successful allocation. Every pre-existing colliding artifact must remain byte-for-byte unchanged; allocation must retain the originally established governed UTC context while changing only the not-yet-created UUID as permitted; and the published Receipt must report the exact retry count in IDENTITY_COLLISION_RETRIES.

Day 060 H-09 success-timeline acceptance

Every retained successful Receipt fixture must satisfy the W002-RCP-006 temporal invariant using its actual embedded UTC tokens. Acceptance must mechanically prove:

  • the invoked WKO UTC is less than or equal to RUN_STARTED_UTC;
  • every non-Receipt governed artifact successfully published by that Run has a governed artifact/transaction UTC between RUN_STARTED_UTC and RUN_FINISHED_UTC, inclusive;
  • RUN_FINISHED_UTC is less than or equal to the Receipt filename/RECEIPT_UTC; and
  • no fixture relies on an artifact timestamp that occurs after the Receipt that claims it, or before the Run that created it.

A controlled-clock acceptance seam may be used to make equality and strict-order cases deterministic, but the fixture generator must not alter timestamps after the fact merely to satisfy the checker.

Day 060 H-11 successful RID_ACTION acceptance

A successful new-Store materialization Receipt may report RID_ACTION: CREATED only because the RID was actually promoted into its final governed RID identity during that Run. A successful existing-Store materialization Receipt reports RID_ACTION: REUSED and the exact inherited RID filename; no new RID candidate is created for that Run.

W002-RCP-ACC-002

Refusal Receipt acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A saved WKO that is actually Run and deterministically refuses must still produce one canonical TXT Receipt when Receipt publication itself remains available. The emitted bytes must conform to the closed RESULT vocabulary, the four governed absence tokens, the exact operation-specific key spelling/order, and the refusal matrix in W002-RCP-006 through W002-RCP-008.

Acceptance must include byte-exact golden Receipt fixtures for every distinct refusal-boundary row required to exercise the serialization matrix for each of the seven executable WASM-002 operations: MATERIALIZE, INVENTORY, UPDATE_ALIASES, REPAIR_MAP, REPAIR_WORK_ORDER_REGISTRY, CONVERT_WINDOWS_1252_TO_UTF_8, and CATALOG_STORES. Multiple Diagnostic IDs that map to the same refusal boundary and the same serialization row do not require duplicate byte fixtures merely because the Diagnostic ID differs.

Acceptance must additionally include one byte-exact UNKNOWN_OPERATION refusal fixture proving the common envelope, OPERATION: UNKNOWN_OPERATION, RESULT: REFUSED, the exact diagnostic ID, absence of any operation-specific section, and immediate CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT: 0.

Fixtures must prove that NONE, NOT_RUN, NOT_AVAILABLE, and NOT_APPLICABLE retain distinct meanings; an established zero count is serialized as 0; no candidate filename is reported as a published identity; and every indexed key uses its complete frozen name and the minimum-three-digit/no-maximum suffix rule.

An unsaved WIP must be proven unable to Run and therefore must not create an execution Receipt.

F-16 materialization-refusal fixtures: byte-exact MATERIALIZE refusal Receipts must exercise the new compatibility pair in all four applicable states: NOT_RUN when Stage 1 did not fail; COMPATIBLE plus NOT_APPLICABLE offset; INCOMPATIBLE plus the exact first undefined-byte offset; and NOT_AVAILABLE / NOT_AVAILABLE when an independent compatibility-read failure prevents a conclusion.

F-23 Receipt-publication failure fixture, reconciled by F-33: a controlled filesystem-fault seam must make canonical RCP publication fail after the underlying analytical/refusal outcome has been established. Acceptance must prove the W002-RCP-010 boundary exactly: no final RCP is fabricated or claimed, any retained candidate evidence follows the governed SCR retention/non-authority rules in W002-STOR-023.1, no RCV artifact is emitted, the user-facing diagnostic distinguishes analytical outcome from Receipt-persistence failure, and already committed analytical artifacts are not retroactively falsified solely because RCP persistence failed.

F-23 ultimate identity-allocation failure fixture: with Receipt publication itself still available, a controlled identity-allocation seam must force a governed operation artifact to exhaust/fail safe allocation. The operation must refuse without overwriting or mutating any colliding pre-existing artifact, and the refusal Receipt/diagnostic evidence must preserve the established collision/allocation-failure facts under PB-STOR-011 and W002-STOR-007.3.

Day 060 H-02 fixture binding: the retained golden corpus must use RECEIPT_VERSION: 1 and the fixture-pinned diagnostic allocations in W002-HELP-001.8. The corpus must contain one success Receipt for each of the seven executable operations, one refusal Receipt for every distinct refusal-boundary row in W002-RCP-007/W002-RCP-008, the three additional Stage-1 compatibility variants needed to cover COMPATIBLE, INCOMPATIBLE, and NOT_AVAILABLE after UTF-8 failure, and one UNKNOWN_OPERATION Receipt. Publication-refusal fixtures may use the operation-specific H-02 publication diagnostic and a non-zero IDENTITY_COLLISION_RETRIES value to satisfy the ultimate identity-allocation-failure acceptance boundary without inventing a second diagnostic solely for the same serialization row.

Day 060 H-09 refusal-timeline acceptance

Every retained refusal Receipt fixture must also satisfy the W002-RCP-006 temporal invariant. For a refusal with no successfully published non-Receipt artifact, acceptance proves WKO_UTC ≤ RUN_STARTED_UTC ≤ RUN_FINISHED_UTC ≤ RECEIPT_UTC. If a refusal legitimately leaves one or more successfully committed non-Receipt artifacts from an already-completed stage, each such artifact UTC must fall between Run start and Run finish and must be listed truthfully under the governing created-artifact rules.

Day 060 H-11 / BM-08 RID_ACTION refusal acceptance

Byte-exact MATERIALIZE refusal acceptance must distinguish new-Store and existing-Store RID paths:

  • new-Store validation, Stage 1, Stage 2, and post-Stage-2 gate refusals before successful RID promotion serialize RID_ACTION: NOT_RUN and do not serialize a candidate as a published RID;
  • a controlled new-Store refusal after RID promotion has successfully completed may serialize RID_ACTION: CREATED together with the exact published RID filename, but only if that RID was actually promoted and the remaining refusal/rollback evidence is truthful under the publication rules;
  • an existing-Store refusal after the inherited RID has been selected and validated serializes RID_ACTION: REUSED and the exact inherited RID filename even when Stage 1, Stage 2, a later gate, or publication subsequently refuses;
  • an existing lineage whose required inherited RID cannot be validly established serializes RID_ACTION: NOT_AVAILABLE and RID_FILENAME: NOT_AVAILABLE rather than claiming reuse.

Acceptance must specifically reject the historical H-02 fixture pattern that reported RID_ACTION: CREATED while no RID existed and CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT: 0.

Day 060 H-12 H-02 publication-diagnostic scope

The H-02 operation-specific publication diagnostics whose required facts are artifact_class and collision_retry_count are acceptance pins for governed filename identity-allocation collision exhaustion. They are not catch-all Diagnostic IDs for unrelated publication failures such as chronology guards, write/close/rename failures, or malformed predecessor state. Those distinct conditions use their own registry allocations; DS-UTC-001 is independently frozen for the strict monotonic-UTC guard.

Day 060 H-13 / BM-10 zero-byte and BOM-only NO_HEADER_RECORD Receipt fixtures

The retained golden corpus must contain two distinct byte-exact MATERIALIZE refusal Receipts for the P3-09 no-header boundary:

  • Zero-byte source: the bound source has exact certified byte count 0; Stage 1 passes; Stage 2 refuses with CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION: NO_HEADER_RECORD; CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET: 0; CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE: 1; CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD: 1; and CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL: 1.
  • UTF-8-BOM-only source: the bound source consists exactly of bytes EF BB BF and has exact certified byte count 3; Stage 1 passes; Stage 2 refuses with CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION: NO_HEADER_RECORD; CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET: 3; CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE: 1; CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD: 1; and CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL: 1.

These two Receipt fixtures must carry their own truthful source filenames, Work Order identities, run timestamps, Receipt identities, and other governed facts. Only the five-field CSV refusal tuple has the narrower relationship stated in W002-RCP-007; the complete Receipt files are not otherwise required to be byte-identical.

Day 060 H-14 / BM-11 CONVERT undefined-byte Receipt binding

The coordinated golden Receipt corpus must include the byte-exact CONVERT_WINDOWS_1252_TO_UTF_8 refusal fixture from W002-CONV-ACC-002 using source bytes 41 81 42. Its Receipt must carry UNDEFINED_WINDOWS_1252_BYTE_OFFSET: 1 and the exact pre-transcoding refusal values frozen in W002-RCP-008.

W002-RCP-ACC-003

Receipt TXT is invariant to presentation state in WASM-002

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The same governed run must be exercised under materially different permitted browser presentation states. In each case the run Receipt must remain an RCP TXT artifact governed by the same receipt serialization and facts. Presentation must not convert it to HTML or alter execution truth in WASM-002.

This acceptance gate does not require a configurable Brand Manifest; that capability is deferred.

WASM-002 Store RID Spine

The RID artifact is the permanent row spine of a Store. It exists so later aligned columns can be reasoned about, reused, combined, filtered, enriched, and eventually assembled into deliverables without repeatedly rebuilding or renumbering the underlying row universe. Revision AO freezes only the row-identity contract required by WASM-002; later filtering, calculated-column, join, and BUILD CSV operations may rely on this contract without being pulled into WASM-002 scope merely by this section.

W002-RID-001

A Suitcase may contain multiple Stores and each current Store state binds exactly one RID

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The Suitcase is a workspace and may contain zero, one, or multiple logical Stores. Every committed Store state binds exactly one governed current RID artifact. RID values are unique only within their Store row universe; they are not Suitcase-global identifiers.

Ordinary same-row-universe work reuses that RID unchanged. In WASM-002, a missing, unreadable, or invalid current RID makes the Store INVALID; no executable WASM-002 operation regenerates or substitutes that RID. Read-only Help/evidence may explain analyst-owned restoration or lineage-retirement choices, but Data Sculptor does not publish a replacement RID.

The stable logical row reference in WASM-002 is conceptually (Store lineage, RID value); the current physical RID identity is the exact rid_filename bound by the authoritative MAP.

W002-RID-002

The Store RID is generated automatically once and reused unchanged in WASM-002

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

When the first successful materialization establishes a new Store, Data Sculptor must automatically generate that Store's initial RID artifact as part of the same Stage 2 operation and the same all-or-refuse publication boundary. The analyst does not separately request ordinary RID generation.

Before the RID SCR candidate is created, Data Sculptor establishes the materialization publication-transaction UTC under PB-STOR-013/PB-STOR-014 and allocates a RID-specific UUID. The canonical RID byte stream is then written as the visible governed SCR candidate whose filename already carries that exact UTC, UUID, and .csv extension intended for the final RID identity. Requested materialized columns likewise begin as governed SCR candidates whose distinct COL-specific UUIDs are allocated before those candidates are opened under the same transaction UTC. The new RID candidate and all requested COL candidates must reach EOF, reconcile to the same accepted Store row count N, and pass their required final validation before any candidate is promoted.

After complete-set validation, Data Sculptor promotes the RID candidate first by host rename that changes only the three-letter semantic class token from SCR to RID. The candidate bytes, UTC token, UUID, and .csv extension must remain unchanged across that promotion. Requested COL candidates are promoted only after RID promotion succeeds. If later promotion or successor-MAP publication prevents transaction commit, the newly promoted RID is not committed Store state merely because an RID-looking file exists; it must be rolled back where safely possible or retained as attributable recovery evidence under the materialization failure contract.

A first Store-establishing materialization commits exactly one RID regardless of how many requested COLs are materialized. Later ordinary materializations and other same-row-universe WASM-002 operations must reuse that RID unchanged. They must not create a new RID candidate, regenerate, replace, renumber, or silently supersede the inherited RID.

RID reconstruction/replacement is not an executable WASM-002 operation. Any future governed RID-recovery design remains deferred and must be reintroduced by an explicit later PRD freeze.

W002-RID-003

RID physical identity uses the governed RID filename grammar

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The physical RID filename must be:

__DS__RID__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv

The filename contains governed physical identity only. A Store name or friendly analyst alias must not be inserted into, substituted for, or used to rename this immutable physical RID filename.

W002-RID-004

RID is a canonical one-column CSV containing the exact sequence 1 through N

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The RID artifact must serialize as a canonical one-column UTF-8 CSV with:

  • exactly one UTF-8 BOM at byte zero;
  • a structural first logical record exactly N=<value>, where <value> is the canonical unsigned base-10 representation of the Store's total logical data-row count N;
  • uppercase N, exactly one equals sign, no spaces, no sign, no leading zeroes except the single digit 0, and no separators or locale formatting;
  • LF (0x0A) record terminators on every supported host;
  • exactly N data records after the header, containing the consecutive unquoted decimal integers 1 through N in order;
  • no zero RID data value, negatives, signs, thousands separators, decimal points, exponent notation, or leading zeroes; and
  • a final LF after the last record. For N=0, the canonical bytes are the UTF-8 BOM followed by N=0 and LF, with no data records.

The N=<value> record is structural metadata and does not consume a Store row. The governed RID artifact class/filename and Store MAP binding identify the artifact as a RID; the literal header RID is not used by the frozen WASM-002 serialization.

W002-RID-005

RID cardinality and order define same-Store column alignment

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

If a Store RID contains N data records, every governed column claimed to be aligned to that Store must contain exactly N data records in the same RID order. Data Sculptor must not describe a shorter, longer, reordered, duplicated, or row-shifted column as aligned to that Store.

This invariant applies to materialized source columns in WASM-002 and is the stable contract that later calculated, Boolean-selection, verification, or left-join enrichment columns may rely upon.

W002-RID-006

A different row universe requires a different Store and a new RID

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An operation that changes which rows exist or changes their governed order does not mutate the existing Store RID. It establishes a different row universe and therefore requires a new logical Store identity and a new RID artifact beginning again at 1 for that new Store.

Filtering that is represented only as a same-length aligned Boolean/selection column does not itself change the row universe; building a new reduced/reordered row set later would.

W002-RID-007

The Store MAP gives RID a friendly alias without changing RID identity

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The physical RID artifact remains identified by its immutable governed filename and semantic RID class. Every valid Store MAP records that exact rid_filename and one current human-facing rid_alias.

Changing the RID alias must not rename, rewrite, regenerate, or alter the meaning of the RID artifact. The same Store MAP also records the Store alias and materialized-column aliases, so the analyst-facing names and the physical Store spine remain explicitly connected in one visible governed artifact.

W002-RID-008

Ordinary RID generation is implicit Store infrastructure; RID reconstruction is deferred

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

WASM-002 materialization Work Orders specify the analyst's requested source columns and aliases. They must not require or expose a separate instruction such as RID, ROW INDEX, GENERATE RID, or an equivalent switch to create the Store row spine.

Initial RID generation for a new Store is mandatory engine behavior implied by successful MATERIALIZE. WASM-002 must not provide an option to disable it. When ordinary materialization extends an existing Store, the engine must recognize and reuse that Store's existing RID.

If that bound RID is missing or invalid, the Store is INVALID and ordinary Store operations refuse. WASM-002 exposes no RECOVER RID executable syntax. A future explicit recovery design may be considered in V1-BACKLOG, but it is not part of this build contract.

W002-RID-009

Future RID recovery eligibility model is deferred

DEFERRED
SCOPEV1-BACKLOGBUILD—

This requirement preserves an earlier candidate model for reconstructing a damaged physical RID from surviving governed Store evidence. It is deferred to V1-BACKLOG and imposes no executable WASM-002 behavior.

For WASM-002, a missing, unreadable, or invalid current RID makes the Store INVALID; Data Sculptor does not infer a replacement RID from COL cardinality. If recovery is reconsidered later, the future design must explicitly freeze how one target Store is identified, what evidence proves the same logical row axis, and when recovery must refuse rather than guess.

W002-RID-010

Future RID recovery publication model is deferred

DEFERRED
SCOPEV1-BACKLOGBUILD—

The immutable replacement-RID/successor-MAP publication model previously described here is deferred to V1-BACKLOG. WASM-002 never publishes a replacement RID for an existing Store lineage.

A future recovery design, if adopted, must preserve prior artifacts, use an all-or-refuse governed publication boundary, define the Store-lineage continuity evidence explicitly, and record any old-to-new RID transition durably. None of those future semantics are executable obligations in WASM-002.

W002-RID-ACC-001

Canonical RID byte serialization acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An acceptance fixture with N=5 must prove exact governed bytes equivalent to a UTF-8 BOM followed by:

N=5
1
2
3
4
5

Every record uses LF termination and the file ends with a final LF. A separate N=0 fixture must prove exact bytes equivalent to UTF-8 BOM + N=0 and no data records. The N=5 fixture repeated under different permitted source-window boundaries must produce byte-identical RID content apart from the governed physical filename allocated to the artifact. Full RID validation must also prove that the declared N, the number of following data records, and the exact sequence 1..N agree.

W002-RID-ACC-002

Multiple Stores in one Suitcase retain independent RID spines

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An acceptance fixture must establish at least two Stores with different row counts in the same Suitcase and prove that each Store publishes and retains exactly one distinct governed RID artifact. RID values may overlap numerically across Stores without collision because the Store identity disambiguates them.

W002-RID-ACC-003

Later same-Store materialization reuses rather than regenerates RID

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An acceptance fixture must establish a Store with an initial materialization, record the physical RID identity and exact RID bytes, then perform a later permitted materialization that adds at least one aligned COL without changing the row universe. The later run must reference and reuse the original RID artifact; no replacement RID may be published and the original RID bytes must remain unchanged.

W002-RID-ACC-004

Implicit RID generation acceptance for single- and multi-column first materialization

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Acceptance must execute two Store-establishing Work Orders that contain no RID or row-index syntax: one requesting exactly one source column and one requesting multiple source columns. Each successfully committed run must publish exactly one governed RID artifact regardless of the number of requested COL artifacts.

The fixture must prove that RID creation occurs during the same Stage 2 source-record traversal that establishes the Store row count rather than by requiring a second source pass solely to construct RID. The RID row count must reconcile exactly with every requested COL row count and the final accepted Store N.

Before RID candidate creation, acceptance must prove that the publication-transaction UTC and RID-specific UUID are already established, and that the governed SCR filename carries exactly the UTC, UUID, and .csv extension intended for the final RID identity. Before complete-set validation, the RID bytes must exist only as that governed SCR candidate. Acceptance must prove that the RID candidate is promoted by host rename only after the complete RID/COL candidate set validates, that the physical-name change is exactly the class token SCR to RID, that candidate bytes/UTC/UUID/extension are unchanged across promotion, that RID promotion precedes COL promotion, and that the resulting RID is not considered committed Store membership until the successor MAP is successfully promoted and binds that exact RID filename.

W002-RID-ACC-005

Future RID recovery acceptance is deferred

DEFERRED
SCOPEV1-BACKLOGBUILD—

No RID-recovery acceptance fixture is required for WASM-002 because RID reconstruction is not an executable operation in this build.

If a later V1 revision reintroduces governed RID recovery, acceptance must be specified at that time from the newly frozen eligibility, publication, refusal, continuity, Help, and Receipt contracts rather than treating this historical candidate fixture as authoritative.

WASM-002 Suitcase Inventory Snapshot

WASM-002 includes a lightweight explicit inventory operation for ordinary analyst continuity. It records visible file metadata for the authorized flat Suitcase without reading the contents of those files. The inventory is evidence of what filenames and host-reported metadata were visible at one moment; it is deliberately not a cryptographic claim that file bytes are unchanged.

Two assurance levels remain distinct. INVENTORY is the quick metadata-level operation frozen here. Whole-file or whole-Suitcase SHA-256 fingerprinting is a heavier byte-reading operation and is not silently performed by INVENTORY. The later explicit FINGERPRINT workflow may publish immutable LCK Suitcase Lock evidence; INVENTORY does not create, refresh, or verify LCK. Help must explain the distinction.
W002-INV-001

INVENTORY is an explicit standalone WASM-002 Work Order operation

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical WASM-002 form is:

SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS "Inventory this Suitcase"
INVENTORY

INVENTORY reads the authorized Suitcase directory metadata and creates one governed Suitcase Inventory Snapshot. It is read-only with respect to pre-existing Suitcase files. In WASM-002, an INVENTORY Work Order must not also request materialization, conversion, fingerprinting, another analytical operation, or another Work Order invocation.

F-08 structure freeze: after the common SUITCASE: . / WORK ORDER AS "..." preamble, INVENTORY is the sole semantic operation clause and is terminal. No SOURCE, MAP, KEEP, alias mutation, conversion, repair, catalog, or composition clause is valid in the same WKO.

W002-INV-002

Suitcase Inventory uses the governed INV artifact class and canonical filename grammar

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A successful inventory produces exactly one visible flat TXT artifact whose physical filename is:

__DS__INV__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.txt

The UTC and UUID tokens follow the existing governed artifact-identity rules. Data Sculptor must not create an inventory subfolder, hidden cache copy, or alternate private persistence.

F-14 publication: the INV body is produced first under the matching W002-STOR-023.1 SCR identity with the same UTC, UUID and .txt extension intended for the final INV. Publication to INV occurs only after the complete scan and deterministic INV serialization validate successfully.

W002-INV-003

The lightweight inventory records filename, exact byte length, and last-modified metadata

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

For every regular file present in the authorized flat Suitcase root at snapshot time, the inventory must record:

  • the exact visible filename;
  • the exact byte length reported by the host file object; and
  • the host/browser-reported last-modified value rendered in the canonical UTC millisecond form when available.

WASM-002 must not claim access to a true file-creation timestamp. It must not infer, fabricate, or substitute a creation time from the last-modified value. If usable last-modified metadata is unavailable, the inventory must represent that fact explicitly rather than invent a timestamp.

P3-10 last-modified availability test: host/browser last-modified metadata is usable only when the host supplies a finite, non-negative whole-number millisecond value that can be represented in the canonical UTC millisecond timestamp form. If that test fails, the inventory must serialize the governed unavailable value rather than infer, round, substitute, or fabricate a timestamp.

W002-INV-004

INVENTORY does not read file contents or compute content hashes

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The lightweight inventory must be produced from directory enumeration and file metadata only. Data Sculptor must not open and stream the contents of each listed file merely to create the inventory, and it must not compute SHA-256 or another content fingerprint as an implicit side effect.

Its cost should therefore scale primarily with the number of directory entries and metadata calls, not with the aggregate byte size of the files. A 7 GB CSV and a 7 KB CSV each contribute one metadata entry rather than requiring their contents to be read.

W002-INV-005

Inventory scope is the authorized flat Suitcase root

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

WASM-002 inventories regular files and immediate child directory entries in the directory denoted by SUITCASE: .. Data Sculptor must not recursively inspect, enumerate, size, hash, or otherwise inventory the contents of a child directory in this build.

Each immediate child directory is recorded as a directory entry by its exact visible name only. Its nested contents and aggregate size are outside the WASM-002 Inventory contract. This rule preserves the flat-Suitcase storage model while making the presence of user-created directories explicit rather than silently omitting them.

F-26 SOURCE distinction: inclusion in an Inventory is evidence that an entry was physically visible to the Inventory operation; it does not make that entry eligible for a Work Order SOURCE. SOURCE eligibility is the narrower contract in W002-WKO-009.1.

W002-INV-006

Inventory serialization is deterministic UTF-8 TXT

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The INV artifact is a deterministic human-readable TXT document encoded as UTF-8 without BOM, using LF (0x0A) line endings, the same KEY: VALUE line grammar, and the same quoted-text escaping rule frozen by W002-RCP-005. Every INV ends with exactly one final LF, contains no trailing spaces, and contains no blank physical lines.

The exact V1 Inventory serialization order is:

  1. INVENTORY_VERSION
  2. INVENTORY_UTC
  3. WORK_ORDER_FILENAME
  4. SUITCASE
  5. ENTRY_COUNT
  6. for each regular-file entry in deterministic ascending exact-filename UTF-8 byte order, one contiguous indexed triplet: FILE_<INDEX>, FILE_<INDEX>_BYTE_LENGTH, FILE_<INDEX>_LAST_MODIFIED_UTC
  7. DIRECTORY_COUNT
  8. exactly DIRECTORY_COUNT directory-name records using contiguous indexed keys DIRECTORY_<INDEX>, ordered by ascending exact-directory-name UTF-8 bytes.

INVENTORY_VERSION is the unquoted integer 1 for this contract. WORK_ORDER_FILENAME, SUITCASE, each FILE_<INDEX> filename, and each DIRECTORY_<INDEX> name use the common double-quoted UTF-8 text serialization. FILE_<INDEX>_BYTE_LENGTH is the exact non-negative ungrouped ASCII base-10 byte length. FILE_<INDEX>_LAST_MODIFIED_UTC is either the exact canonical UTC millisecond token governed by W002-INV-003 or the unquoted governed absence token NOT_AVAILABLE.

Indexed suffixes are one-based decimal with a minimum width of three digits and no maximum width: 001 through 999 are zero-padded and 1000 onward uses the full ungrouped decimal form. When ENTRY_COUNT or DIRECTORY_COUNT is zero, no indexed lines for that list appear.

ENTRY_COUNT remains the regular-file count. Directory records contain the exact immediate child directory name only and do not imply recursive inspection or a computed directory size. Filename and directory-name representations remain unambiguous even when a name contains whitespace, quotes, or delimiter-like characters because the common quote-doubling rule applies.

P3-10 inventory timestamp binding: INVENTORY_UTC must equal the exact canonical UTC token embedded in the final governed __DS__INV__<UTC>__<uuid-v4>.txt filename, just as RECEIPT_UTC is bound to the governed Receipt filename UTC. The INV body and filename therefore cannot claim different capture times.

W002-INV-007

The current inventory describes the pre-publication Suitcase state and excludes itself

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Data Sculptor must enumerate and fix the inventory snapshot before publishing the new INV artifact. The INV artifact being created is therefore not one of its own listed entries. Any older INV artifact that already existed at snapshot time is an ordinary Suitcase file and is included like any other file.

This pre-publication rule prevents recursive self-reference while preserving an accurate snapshot of the state that existed immediately before the new inventory evidence was added.

W002-INV-008

Help describes INVENTORY as a quick continuity aid, not byte-level proof

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Help must explain that an INV snapshot is useful for ordinary closeout and later orientation: it can reveal additions, removals, renames, size changes, or last-modified changes when snapshots or current metadata are compared. For an unexpected cross-session source problem, Help may direct the analyst to the relevant source entry in an earlier INV and ask whether its filename, exact byte length, or last-modified metadata differs.

Help must also state that unchanged filename/size/last-modified metadata does not prove that file contents or row order are identical. When stronger assurance is warranted because files may change unexpectedly, Help may recommend the explicit later/deeper content-fingerprinting workflow; INVENTORY itself must never imply forensic or cryptographic assurance.

W002-INV-ACC-001

Large-file inventory acceptance proves metadata-only behavior

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An acceptance fixture must place at least one multi-gigabyte file plus several small files in the authorized Suitcase, execute INVENTORY, and prove that the resulting INV records the correct filename, exact byte length, and last-modified metadata without reading the multi-gigabyte file contents.

Evidence must demonstrate that inventory runtime and memory do not scale with the aggregate bytes of the listed files in the way a fingerprinting pass would.

P3-10 metadata determinism: acceptance must include at least one file with usable host last-modified metadata and one test double/fixture in which the last-modified value fails the governed availability test. The first must serialize the exact canonical UTC millisecond value; the second must serialize exactly NOT_AVAILABLE. The accepted INV must also prove that INVENTORY_UTC exactly matches the UTC token in its final INV filename.

Day 060 H-01 byte oracle: acceptance must include at least one byte-exact INV golden fixture using the complete W002-INV-006 key order, indexed suffix rule, quoted-text escaping rule, UTF-8/no-BOM physical form, LF-only line endings, and exactly one final LF. It must include at least two file records so deterministic filename ordering is observable, including one NOT_AVAILABLE last-modified value, and at least one directory record.

Day 060 H-09 reachable-Suitcase INV golden fixture

The byte-exact INV golden fixture used for WASM-002 review must depict a Suitcase state that could actually execute INVENTORY under the current contract rather than an isolated impossible file list.

At minimum, immediately before the Inventory Run begins, the fixture Suitcase contains:

  • one valid current Suitcase Validation Certificate (CER) authorizing the root;
  • one structurally valid current WKO registry MAP;
  • the exact saved immutable INVENTORY WKO referenced by WORK_ORDER_FILENAME, registered as runnable by that current WKO MAP; and
  • the ordinary analyst files used to demonstrate inventory metadata, including the controlled last-modified-available and NOT_AVAILABLE cases.

The INV snapshot is taken before publication of the new INV artifact and before its Receipt publication. Therefore the INV being created and the Receipt for that Run do not appear as pre-existing entries in their own inventory snapshot.

For the retained minimal review fixture, the regular-file ENTRY_COUNT and indexed records must include the CER, current WKO MAP, exact INVENTORY WKO, and the two ordinary sample files, for a total of five regular-file rows, serialized in ascending exact-filename UTF-8 byte order. A later implementation fixture may use different exact governed filenames/UUIDs while preserving the same reachable-state requirement and deterministic ordering.

W002-INV-ACC-002

Inventory snapshot membership and self-exclusion acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An acceptance fixture must include ordinary analyst files, existing governed __DS__ artifacts, and at least one older INV artifact. The new inventory must include every qualifying pre-existing root file in deterministic order, include the older INV, and exclude only the newly generated INV because it did not exist in the fixed pre-publication snapshot.

Adding an unrelated PDF or ZIP before a later inventory must appear as an added inventory entry and must not be treated as an analytical error.

W002-INV-ACC-003

Inventory does not overclaim unchanged contents

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Acceptance documentation and Help fixtures must demonstrate the limitation of metadata-only continuity. A case in which a file's bytes are changed while the observed filename, byte length, and last-modified metadata are preserved or restored must not be described as detectable by INVENTORY alone.

The product must direct the analyst toward stronger explicit fingerprint evidence when byte-level assurance is required.

WASM-002 Governed Storage, Work Order Registry, Store MAPs, Catalog, and Suitcase Validation

Work Order Registry and Governed Publication

W002-STOR-016

Work Order filenames use the governed immutable identity grammar

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

When Data Sculptor saves a new Work Order as a WKO, it shall assign the physical TXT filename. The analyst chooses the validated Suitcase but is not asked to choose or edit the WKO filename.

The exact WKO filename shape is __DS__WKO__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.txt, using UTC at millisecond precision with exactly three millisecond digits and a canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID v4. UTC precedes UUID. If the generated name collides with an existing artifact, PB-STOR-011 governs UUID regeneration and safe retry. The saved WKO thereafter retains that physical identity and remains immutable under W002-STOR-017.

W002-STOR-017

Saved Work Orders are immutable artifacts

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

After a Work Order TXT artifact is saved, Data Sculptor shall not edit, overwrite, or rename that saved Work Order in place. Changing analytical instructions requires saving a new Work Order artifact with a new governed physical identity.

W002-STOR-018

Work Order alias is immutable WKO content and governed MAP metadata

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A human-facing Work Order name is required immutable Work Order content for every executable/saved WASM-002 WKO, not separately editable browser metadata. The canonical declaration is WORK ORDER AS "<alias>" under W002-STEPS-001.1. The quoted alias must be non-empty UTF-8 text and may contain spaces and ordinary phrase punctuation subject to the governed string-literal rules.

After the WKO TXT artifact is saved, Data Sculptor shall not edit the alias in place. Changing the alias, analytical instructions, or comments means creating and saving a new immutable WKO with a new governed physical identity. The physical WKO filename/UUID remains execution identity; the alias is human-facing metadata for display and governed name resolution.

The browser must not maintain a separate mutable Description field or hidden description store. The alias declared by the WKO is also represented in the current governed WKO MAP under W002-STOR-018.1 through W002-STOR-018.4.

W002-STOR-018.1

The existing MAP class includes a distinct WKO alias-registry profile

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Revision BB does not add a new semantic artifact class. The existing MAP class has two explicitly distinguished governed profiles:

  • Store MAP — the existing exact eight-column Store/RID/COL snapshot governed by W002-STOR-019 through W002-STOR-019.12;
  • WKO MAP — a complete immutable snapshot that maps saved Work Order aliases and lifecycle status to exact immutable WKO filenames.

Profile classification is determined by the exact CSV header before profile-specific validation. A valid WKO MAP must never be treated as an eligible Store MAP, and a Store MAP must never be treated as a WKO alias registry. Both remain visible flat-Suitcase MAP artifacts under the canonical immutable filename grammar.

W002-STOR-018.2

WKO MAP schema and serialization are exact and deterministic

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical WKO MAP is UTF-8 CSV without BOM, using LF record termination, with exactly this three-field header:

wko_status,wko_alias,wko_filename

Each row identifies one immutable governed WKO represented in that registry snapshot. wko_status is exactly CURRENT or DEPRECATED. wko_alias is the exact mandatory non-empty alias declared by that WKO's WORK ORDER AS clause. wko_filename is the exact governed physical WKO filename.

Rows are written deterministically by ascending exact UTF-8 byte order of wko_filename. Duplicate wko_filename rows are invalid. Standard governed CSV quoting applies.

For any exact wko_alias value, at most one row may have wko_status=CURRENT; zero or more older rows for that same alias may have wko_status=DEPRECATED. Alias resolution uses the CURRENT row only. A WKO represented by a DEPRECATED row remains immutable historical evidence and is not renamed, rewritten, or deleted merely because its alias target was superseded. A WKO MAP containing more than one CURRENT row for the same exact alias is structurally invalid.

W002-STOR-018.3

Saving a WKO and publishing its WKO MAP binding is one governed save transaction

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Saving a new immutable WKO begins from the current structurally valid WKO MAP in the Suitcase, or an empty WKO registry if no structurally valid WKO MAP exists. Data Sculptor validates the draft, including its mandatory non-empty WORK ORDER AS alias and comment syntax, and checks the governed alias/lifecycle constraints before commit.

F-02 alias-lifecycle decision: if no CURRENT row in the predecessor WKO MAP uses the new WKO's exact alias, the successor registry adds the new WKO as CURRENT. If exactly one CURRENT row already owns that exact alias, Data Sculptor must present exactly two analyst choices before registry commit: Replace alias target or Cancel. Replace alias target constructs the successor WKO MAP by changing the former owner's row to DEPRECATED and adding the newly saved WKO as the sole CURRENT row for that alias; any older DEPRECATED rows remain unchanged. Cancel leaves the predecessor WKO MAP authoritative and does not commit the pending WKO/WKO-MAP pair as a registry update. Data Sculptor must not silently replace the alias target, auto-suffix the alias, or choose between competing owners. A predecessor WKO MAP with more than one CURRENT row for the same alias is structurally invalid under W002-STOR-018.2 and cannot be used as save authority.

The former CURRENT WKO and every prior WKO MAP remain byte-for-byte immutable after replacement. Supersession changes only the lifecycle metadata represented in the newly published successor WKO MAP; it does not edit, rename, delete, or rewrite the historical WKO artifact.

F-14 WKO publication predicate: the new immutable Work Order is first written under the W002-STOR-023.1 SCR identity using the UTC, UUID and .txt extension intended for its final WKO identity. The complete candidate is closed, reopened and validated as a saved WKO: required common preamble, exactly one non-whitespace WORK ORDER AS alias, governed lexical/comment rules, and complete parse under exactly one current WASM-002 executable operation grammar. Only then may the candidate be renamed from SCR to WKO. Save-time current-registry, alias-lifecycle and lifecycle gates remain transaction preconditions. A valid promoted WKO is not yet alias-registry authority; the successor WKO MAP promotion remains the save-transaction commit point.

The WKO is persisted as a new immutable governed WKO artifact and the complete successor WKO MAP is constructed under SCR, closed, reopened, and validated for WKO MAP structural validity: exact profile/schema, exact governed serialization, filename/profile rules, lifecycle-row constraints, and internal row constraints. Whether every referenced physical WKO file is presently visible is a separate registry-health/publication check and is not part of WKO MAP structural validity. For an ordinary successful save transaction, every WKO referenced by the successor registry must be present at publication.

The successor WKO MAP is promoted to MAP last; that successful MAP promotion is the alias-registry commit point for the save transaction. The WKO and successor WKO MAP created by one successful save transaction use one shared canonical transaction UTC while retaining distinct UUIDs.

If successor WKO-MAP structural validation, referenced-file publication checking, or publication itself fails, the save must not be represented as a successfully committed alias-registry update. Data Sculptor must roll back the new WKO out of committed WKO state where safely possible or retain visible non-authoritative SCR failure evidence and report the failure through Help.

F-02 repair-only bootstrap and stale-registry Save boundary

When the current WKO registry is repair-required under W002-STOR-018.4, Data Sculptor may save one ordinary visible immutable WKO whose sole semantic operation is exactly REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY. That saved repair-only WKO may Run by its exact physical WKO filename even though it is not yet represented in the current WKO MAP.

  • The WKO must be structurally valid under the predicate below, must contain exactly one mandatory non-empty WORK ORDER AS, and must contain exactly the governed registry-repair operation and no second operation.
  • The exception does not grant alias-based Run authority. The repair WKO is invoked only by exact physical WKO filename.
  • No other visible but unregistered WKO gains Run eligibility from this exception.
  • The exception ends once registry repair successfully publishes the successor WKO MAP.
  • This is the sole WASM-002 bypass of ordinary current-registry membership for Run eligibility.

Because the registry is already stale, Save of the repair-only WKO does not claim that the WKO has been registered, does not commit an ordinary successor WKO MAP, and does not represent the stale registry as healthy. The new immutable WKO remains visibly unregistered until the repair operation successfully publishes the successor WKO MAP containing its row. Save does not silently perform registry repair.

F-02 governed WKO structural-validity predicate

A visible WKO is structurally valid for registry purposes only when all of the following hold:

  • it is a regular root-level Suitcase file;
  • its physical filename conforms exactly to the governed WKO filename grammar;
  • its bytes are valid UTF-8;
  • LF and CRLF physical line endings are accepted; a lone CR line ending refuses;
  • its content parses completely under exactly one defined WASM-002 executable Work Order grammar;
  • it contains exactly one mandatory non-empty WORK ORDER AS clause;
  • its required common and operation-specific structural clauses are present in their governed order/cardinality; and
  • unknown syntax or prohibited operation mixing causes invalidity/refusal.

Structural validity is not runtime success. A structurally valid WKO remains a valid governed artifact even when a runtime precondition is currently false, such as a referenced source file being absent. Runtime preconditions are checked at Run.

P3-10 repair-bootstrap timing: during REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY, the saved repair-only WKO participates in the bounded discovery performed by that repair run. It is not first “discovered after success.” Its governed registration becomes durable only when the complete successor WKO MAP containing that WKO row is successfully committed. Discovery during the run and registration in the committed successor registry are distinct events.

P2-03 WKO-registry chronology guard: before a save or registry-repair transaction publishes a successor WKO MAP, Data Sculptor establishes the truthful observed transaction UTC and compares it with the chronology predecessor defined by W002-STOR-018.4. The observed UTC must be strictly greater. Equal or earlier UTC refuses before the new WKO/WKO-MAP pair is committed; Data Sculptor must not fabricate a later timestamp, silently wait/retry, skip the predecessor, or select an older registry merely to make publication succeed.

F-13 single-writer pre-commit guard: immediately before the successor WKO MAP promotion that would commit the alias-registry update, Data Sculptor re-resolves the current WKO-registry authority and compares the relevant governing state with the state from which this transaction was derived. If another writing context or external filesystem action has changed that relevant authority, the transaction refuses publication. It must not overwrite the newer registry, silently rebase the pending save, or choose an older registry to make the commit succeed. The existing rollback / attributable SCR recovery-evidence rules apply to any WKO or candidate bytes already produced.

If the save later refuses and an SCR candidate or other attributable staged evidence cannot be safely removed/restored, W002-STOR-023.1 governs retained SCR evidence and its non-authority boundary; WASM-002 does not emit RCV. An unregistered final WKO left by a failure is a valid immutable WKO artifact but does not become current registry authority merely by existing; the WKO MAP remains authoritative.

W002-STOR-018.4

Current WKO MAP selection is based on structural validity; missing referenced WKOs make the registry repair-required

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

WKO MAP structural validity is distinct from registry health. A WKO MAP is structurally valid when the MAP artifact itself satisfies the governed WKO MAP profile/schema, serialization, filename/profile rules, lifecycle-row constraints, and internal row constraints. The present existence of every physical WKO file named by its rows is not part of WKO MAP structural validity.

Only structurally valid WKO MAP artifacts participate in current-registry selection. Among structurally valid WKO MAPs, the one with the greatest canonical UTC millisecond timestamp is the current WKO MAP snapshot and therefore the current governed Work Order alias registry. If two or more structurally valid WKO MAPs share that greatest timestamp, current-registry selection must refuse rather than break the tie by UUID, discovery order, filesystem modified time, or directory order.

Registry-snapshot authority is distinct from alias-target status inside that snapshot. After the current WKO MAP snapshot is selected, an alias resolves only to its exact row whose wko_status is CURRENT. Rows marked DEPRECATED remain visible historical registry evidence but are not alias-resolution targets. The registry must never use the greatest WKO filename UTC, filesystem modified time, or discovery order to choose between rows for an alias. More than one CURRENT row for the same exact alias makes that WKO MAP structurally invalid under W002-STOR-018.2.

If a newer WKO MAP artifact is structurally malformed, it never becomes current. Data Sculptor uses the greatest earlier structurally valid WKO MAP, if one exists, and reports the malformed newer artifact through Help/evidence surfaces. A malformed newer WKO MAP does not itself make the selected earlier registry repair-required.

The current WKO registry is repair-required exactly when the current structurally valid WKO MAP contains one or more rows whose referenced physical WKO files are missing from the Suitcase. Such a MAP remains current; Data Sculptor must not silently fall back to an older WKO MAP merely because a referenced WKO is missing. This preserves the latest registry authority while making the damage explicit and reachable through the governed REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY path.

F-02 deterministic registry reconciliation

REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY reconciles the current WKO MAP against visible WKO artifacts in the Suitcase and constructs one complete successor WKO MAP deterministically:

  1. Remove every row from the successor whose referenced physical WKO file is missing. A missing WKO is never reconstructed, inferred, copied from history, or replaced automatically by a deprecated WKO.
  2. Discover visible structurally valid WKOs that are absent from the current WKO MAP.
  3. If no surviving CURRENT row owns a discovered WKO's exact alias, register that discovered WKO as CURRENT.
  4. If a surviving CURRENT row already owns that exact alias, register the discovered WKO as DEPRECATED; existing current authority is not silently displaced.
  5. If two or more previously unregistered structurally valid WKOs share the same alias and no surviving CURRENT owner exists, register all of those discovered WKOs as DEPRECATED. Data Sculptor must not choose a winner by UTC, filename, UUID, directory order, discovery order, or filesystem modified time.
