  6. The repair WKO itself participates in the same discovery and registration process during the repair run. Its registration becomes durable only when the complete successor WKO MAP is committed.

Predecessor WKO MAPs and surviving WKO files remain immutable historical evidence. Successor rows remain serialized in ascending exact UTF-8 byte order of wko_filename under W002-STOR-018.2.

Day 060 H-10 / BM-07 registry-repair change-set counts

The registry-repair operation distinguishes the successor registry state from the change set produced by this repair Run. The Receipt's REGISTERED_CURRENT_* and REGISTERED_DEPRECATED_* fields describe only the latter.

  • REGISTERED_CURRENT_COUNT is the exact number of previously unregistered structurally valid WKO files newly added by this repair Run with wko_status=CURRENT.
  • REGISTERED_CURRENT_WKO_<INDEX>_FILENAME lists exactly those newly registered CURRENT WKOs, ordered by ascending exact UTF-8 filename bytes.
  • REGISTERED_DEPRECATED_COUNT is the exact number of previously unregistered structurally valid WKO files newly added by this repair Run with wko_status=DEPRECATED.
  • REGISTERED_DEPRECATED_WKO_<INDEX>_FILENAME lists exactly those newly registered DEPRECATED WKOs, ordered by ascending exact UTF-8 filename bytes.
  • Surviving rows that were already present in the base WKO MAP are not counted in either REGISTERED_* total, even though they appear in the successor WKO MAP.
  • Rows removed because their referenced WKO is missing are represented only by REMOVED_STALE_ROW_COUNT and the corresponding stale-WKO filename list; they are not also reflected in either registered count.
  • The bootstrap repair WKO participates exactly like any other newly discovered structurally valid unregistered WKO. If the repair commits it, that exact WKO must appear in one and only one of the two registered filename lists according to the ordinary alias-ownership rules.

These counts therefore answer “what did this repair register?” rather than “how many CURRENT/DEPRECATED rows exist in the resulting registry?”.

F-02 Run eligibility and alias authority

  • Run by human-facing alias resolves only to the sole CURRENT WKO for that alias.
  • A registered CURRENT WKO may Run by exact physical WKO filename, subject to ordinary runtime preconditions.
  • A registered DEPRECATED WKO may also Run by exact physical WKO filename, subject to ordinary runtime preconditions, to support deliberate historical reproduction.
  • An unregistered WKO may not Run merely because its file is visible, except for the single bounded repair-only bootstrap in W002-STOR-018.3.

The browser may use the current structurally valid WKO MAP to show human-facing Work Order aliases together with read-only CURRENT/DEPRECATED lifecycle state while keeping exact physical WKO filenames visible/inspectable. Future Work Order composition may use the same registry to resolve a non-empty alias to exactly one immutable WKO artifact through its sole CURRENT row. This requirement does not pull deferred Work Order invocation/orchestration grammar into WASM-002; it establishes the governed alias-registry selection, lifecycle, and repair boundary that later composition can depend on.

F-08 REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY Work Order structure:

SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS "Repair Work Order Registry"
REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY

After the common preamble, REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY is the sole semantic operation clause and is terminal. It takes no analyst-supplied SOURCE, Store MAP, alias-mutation list, column selector, conversion source, or catalog clause. Its bounded unregistered-repair bootstrap remains governed by W002-STOR-018.3. The DS-STEPS phrase is distinct from the Receipt operation token REPAIR_WORK_ORDER_REGISTRY.

P2-03 chronology predecessor: for any WKO-registry successor publication, the chronology predecessor is the unique current structurally valid WKO MAP immediately before that publication transaction. It is the MAP selected by the current-registry rule above, not an older registry used for inspection and not a filesystem-modified-time surrogate. If no structurally valid WKO MAP exists and the operation is legitimately establishing the first governed registry state, there is no predecessor UTC.

Future-dated current WKO MAP: a structurally valid current WKO MAP whose governed UTC is later than truthful observed host UTC remains the current registry; the timestamp conflict does not by itself make the MAP malformed or repair-required. Successor WKO-MAP publication is blocked until the monotonic UTC precondition can be satisfied. Help must identify the exact blocking WKO MAP and explain the analyst-owned exits: correct an incorrect host clock; wait/rerun after truthful time advances beyond the predecessor; or, when the analyst deliberately determines that the active future-dated WKO MAP should no longer govern the Suitcase, move that exact MAP out of the active Suitcase root and reopen/rescan. That filesystem action is not a Data Sculptor repair operation. It may expose an older structurally valid WKO MAP as current, and restoring the moved future-dated MAP to the active Suitcase may make it current again under the ordinary greatest-UTC rule.

Store MAP Lineage and Health

W002-STOR-019

Store state is preserved as visible immutable MAP history

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Each valid WASM-002 MAP is one complete immutable Store snapshot in the same flat Suitcase. Store state is not stored in hidden browser persistence and is not represented by a mutable well-known singleton.

Each successful Store-establishing materialization or later governed Store-metadata/materialized-column update publishes a new immutable MAP under the canonical __DS__MAP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv identity grammar. Earlier MAP artifacts remain visible history and are not overwritten or deleted merely because a newer Store state is created.

Day 057 CAT reconciliation: the one-Store-per-MAP invariant is unchanged. A collection of independently MAP-governed Stores may additionally be summarized by a governed CAT Store Catalog for collection-level discovery and orientation. CAT does not govern Store semantics, lineage, health, repair, inheritance, or current-MAP selection. MAP remains authoritative for each Store.

W002-STOR-019.1

A Work Order may explicitly select at most one Store MAP

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Each governed Work Order may explicitly identify at most one valid immutable Store MAP as its Store/inheritance base. If more than one MAP is explicitly specified, Data Sculptor must refuse before Store resolution, alias resolution, materialization, or mutation.

An explicitly named valid MAP binds the run to exactly the Store identified by that MAP's rid_filename and overrides automatic Store-MAP discovery even when newer MAPs for that Store or other Stores exist.

W002-STOR-019.2

Without an explicit MAP, materialization performs Store-aware MAP inheritance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

If a materializing Work Order does not explicitly identify a MAP, Data Sculptor must compare the exact Work Order SOURCE filename with the one common exact source_filename carried by every row of each routable Store lineage's structurally valid Store MAP. That common source_filename is the Store lineage's source identity for WASM-002 routing. The redundant ninth Store-source field from the superseded profile is not part of the canonical Store MAP.

P3-07 routing term: for automatic source routing, a routable Store lineage is a Store lineage for which at least one structurally valid Store MAP exists, regardless of whether the lineage currently evaluates VALID, DEGRADED, or INVALID. Routing discovery must use this term rather than the ambiguous word eligible. Store health is evaluated only after the lineage has been discovered.

  • If no routable Store lineage exists for the exact source filename, Data Sculptor may establish a new Store with a new RID and first Store MAP only if the active Suitcase contains no structurally malformed Store-MAP-class artifact.
  • If exactly one routable Store lineage exists, Data Sculptor routes to that lineage. If its current state permits materialization, the current governed Store MAP is the inheritance base; if its current state is DEGRADED or INVALID, ordinary materialization refuses under the damaged-lineage rules below.
  • If more than one distinct routable Store lineage exists for the same exact source filename, automatic inheritance must refuse rather than guess which Store the analyst intended. The analyst must explicitly select one permitted MAP.

All-Store-MAPs-damaged guard: if exact-SOURCE routing finds no routable Store lineage but one or more structurally malformed Store-MAP-class artifacts are present in the active Suitcase, ordinary materialization must refuse before creating a new Store or RID. Data Sculptor must not infer that the absence of a structurally valid Store MAP proves that no prior Store lineage existed. Help must identify the malformed Store MAP artifact or artifacts that caused this guard. A damaged MAP therefore cannot silently turn Store damage into permission to create a replacement lineage.

Store lineages are distinguished by their governed lineage identity. Current-MAP selection and Store-health evaluation are separate governed questions under this requirement and W002-STOR-019.10. If two or more structurally valid current MAP candidates for the one routed Store share the greatest canonical UTC millisecond timestamp, automatic inheritance must refuse rather than infer chronology from UUID, directory order, filesystem modified time, or discovery order.

F-03 canonical evaluated Store-health states

Store health is evaluated from the current structurally valid Store MAP and the presently visible governed artifacts it references, using the applicable validation tier in W002-STOR-019.10. WASM-002 has exactly three evaluated Store-health states:

  • VALID — the current Store MAP is structurally valid; the referenced RID is valid; and every mapped non-RID COL is valid.
  • DEGRADED — the current Store MAP is structurally valid; the referenced RID is valid; and one or more mapped non-RID COL artifacts are missing or invalid.
  • INVALID — the current Store MAP is structurally valid, but its referenced RID is missing or invalid.

There is no fourth ABANDONED Store-health status in WASM-002.

F-03 status is evaluated, not persisted

VALID, DEGRADED, and INVALID are evaluated states. WASM-002 does not write or maintain a mutable persisted Store-status flag.

While a Store evaluates INVALID, Data Sculptor exposes no governed Store-recovery operation for that Store and never regenerates, substitutes, or infers a replacement RID. If the exact governed RID physical identity becomes visible again through analyst-owned external restoration and passes the validation tier required by the next operation, the Store is re-evaluated from the visible governed artifacts and may become VALID or DEGRADED. That is re-evaluation, not RID recovery by Data Sculptor.

F-03 strict DEGRADED operation gate

When a Store evaluates DEGRADED, REPAIR MAP is the only enabled Store mutation operation for that lineage.

  • ordinary materialization into that Store refuses;
  • extension with new columns refuses;
  • alias mutation refuses;
  • transformations and other Store mutations refuse;
  • read-only Help, Inventory, status/orientation surfaces, CAT orientation, and evidence inspection remain available subject to their own contracts.

F-03 no damaged-lineage fork

If exact SOURCE routing identifies a lineage whose current Store evaluates DEGRADED, ordinary materialization refuses and directs the analyst to the governed REPAIR MAP path. If the routed Store evaluates INVALID, ordinary materialization refuses and WASM-002 provides no RID-recovery path. Neither condition permits Data Sculptor to treat the source as unseen or establish a replacement Store with a new RID for that routed lineage.

Damaged-lineage routing: exact SOURCE routing must not treat a known damaged lineage as unseen merely because its current Store state cannot accept ordinary materialization. If routing identifies a DEGRADED or INVALID lineage, ordinary materialization refuses rather than silently creating a replacement Store for that same routed lineage.

Help duty for an all-COLs-broken DEGRADED lineage: when the current structurally valid Store MAP references a valid RID but every mapped non-RID COL is missing or invalid, REPAIR MAP cannot publish a zero-COL successor and must refuse. Help must identify the exact blocked Store lineage and current MAP, then explain these analyst-owned exits: (1) externally restore at least one governed COL artifact under its original physical filename; Data Sculptor then applies the governed validation tier required by the next operation before the artifact can re-enter use, so Store health can be re-evaluated and REPAIR MAP may become available; (2) rename the analyst-owned source and materialize the renamed source to deliberately begin a new Store lineage with a new RID, without repairing, replacing, or erasing the damaged lineage; or (3) retire the damaged lineage from active Suitcase routing by moving all Store MAP artifacts belonging to that lineage out of the Suitcase root. Help must warn that moving only the latest MAP is insufficient because an older structurally valid MAP could otherwise become current.

Help duty for an INVALID lineage: when the current structurally valid Store MAP references a missing or invalid RID, Help must identify the exact blocked Store lineage and current MAP, state that WASM-002 does not silently regenerate or substitute a RID as part of ordinary materialization, and explain these analyst-owned exits: (1) externally restore a governed RID artifact under its original physical filename; Data Sculptor then applies the governed validation tier required by the next operation before the artifact can re-enter use, so Store health can be re-evaluated; (2) rename the analyst-owned source and materialize the renamed source to deliberately begin a new Store lineage with a new RID while leaving the damaged lineage untouched; or (3) retire the damaged lineage from active Suitcase routing by moving all Store MAP artifacts belonging to that lineage out of the Suitcase root, again warning that moving only the latest MAP is insufficient.

Renaming the source and retiring a lineage are distinct analyst choices. Renaming preserves the damaged lineage in the Suitcase and creates a separate lineage under a different source identity. Moving all lineage MAPs out removes that lineage from active routing while preserving the moved artifacts wherever the analyst chooses to keep them. These are analyst filesystem actions, not new Data Sculptor recovery operations.

Assurance boundary: exact source-filename matching in this rule is a Store-routing/orientation mechanism, not proof that an analyst-owned source has identical bytes or row order across separate sessions. Ordinary WASM-002 materialization must not silently represent that filename equality as cryptographic continuity.

P3-08 CVT source-identity boundary: a governed CVT is a new immutable source artifact whose Store-routing source identity is its exact physical CVT filename. Two different CVT filenames are different source identities even when both conversions began from analyst-owned files having the same original filename. WASM-002 does not carry the analyst-owned pre-conversion filename forward as hidden Store-lineage identity and does not infer continuity between separate CVT artifacts. First materialization of a CVT therefore establishes or routes only by that exact CVT filename under the normal rules above.

P2-03 current Store-MAP chronology: within one routable Store lineage, the current structurally valid Store MAP is the unique structurally valid MAP carrying the greatest canonical UTC millisecond timestamp. If two or more structurally valid MAPs share that greatest timestamp, current authority is ambiguous and selection refuses rather than using UUID or discovery order. This current MAP is also the lineage's chronology predecessor for any new successor publication, even when the operation explicitly derives its requested new state from an older historical MAP.

F-15 exact-source comparison and routing domain: the Work Order SOURCE value and each Store MAP's common source_filename are compared by exact Unicode scalar-value sequence under PB-STOR-010, with no case folding or Unicode normalization. Automatic routing compares only routable Store lineages whose structurally valid Store MAPs participate in that exact-source routing decision. Unrelated Suitcase files, non-Store artifact classes, filesystem enumeration order, and arrival order are outside the routing comparison domain and cannot create or remove a source match.

W002-STOR-019.3

Any valid historical Store MAP may be selected explicitly with MAP "<filename>"

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A governed Store-aware Work Order may explicitly identify any one structurally valid immutable Store MAP present in the Suitcase, including an older snapshot when newer MAPs for that Store also exist. The canonical clause is:

MAP "__DS__MAP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv"

The quoted value must be the exact physical filename of one valid Store MAP. A WKO MAP profile, missing file, malformed MAP, or other MAP profile is invalid for this clause. Data Sculptor uses exactly the named Store MAP rather than silently substituting a later one.

For materialization, SOURCE "..." remains required to identify the source file being read; the optional MAP "..." clause occurs immediately after SOURCE and before KEEP, overrides automatic Store-MAP inheritance, and supplies the exact Store-state base. The Work Order's exact SOURCE filename must match the selected lineage's governed source identity under the frozen source/Store compatibility rules or validation refuses. For an alias-only UPDATE ALIASES Work Order, MAP "..." may itself be the Store-state selector and no source-data read is required.

Historical-MAP health gate. Explicit selection of a current or historical Store MAP never bypasses current Store-lineage health. The selected lineage must currently evaluate VALID, and every RID/COL binding referenced by the named MAP must currently be present and valid. If either condition fails, Data Sculptor refuses the operation. An older MAP cannot be used to hide present lineage damage. The same rule applies when UPDATE ALIASES uses a historical Store MAP as its base.

Once selected, the exact MAP identity, Store RID binding, Store alias, RID alias, and materialized-column mapping state remain fixed for the governed run. The MAP filename is execution input, not a friendly alias.

P2-03 base-versus-predecessor distinction: an explicitly selected historical MAP is the operation's base MAP—the Store snapshot from which requested new state is derived. It does not become the chronology predecessor merely because it was selected. If the operation publishes a new Store MAP, the chronology predecessor remains the Store lineage's current structurally valid MAP immediately before publication. The new transaction UTC must be strictly greater than that current MAP UTC. This preserves one chronological MAP history rather than creating a branch from the historical base.

F-21 current-state consequence: merely selecting or validating a historical Store MAP does not change Store authority. If the governed run refuses or otherwise publishes no successor Store MAP, the lineage's pre-run current MAP remains current. If the run successfully publishes a successor derived from a historical base, that new MAP enters the same single chronological history and ordinary greatest-governed-UTC current-state selection applies. Because successor publication already requires a truthful transaction UTC strictly greater than the pre-publication chronology predecessor, the successfully published successor becomes current. The explicitly selected historical base and the formerly current MAP both remain immutable historical evidence.

This behavior is deliberate state derivation, not a branch, rollback-in-place, overwrite, or mutation of prior MAPs. The operation base records which Store snapshot supplied the requested starting state; chronology records when the new governed state was published. Those are distinct facts.

W002-STOR-019.4

Store MAPs are complete snapshots, not delta logs

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Each valid Store MAP represents one complete usable Store metadata and materialized-column mapping state for that version. It must not require replaying a chain of earlier MAP files merely to reconstruct the Store's current RID binding, aliases, or materialized-column mappings.

A newer MAP created from an inherited older MAP contains the complete resulting Store snapshot after applying the governed Work Order's successful changes.

W002-STOR-019.5

Materialization or governed Store metadata mutation emits one successor MAP

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

When a governed Work Order materializes one or more columns or requests governed Store/RID/COL alias changes, Data Sculptor begins from the applicable governed Store-state base. Ordinary materialization uses the explicitly selected MAP or Store-aware automatic inheritance under W002-STOR-019.2. A new Store begins from newly established Store/RID metadata plus an empty materialized-column mapping set before requested materialization is applied.

All successful updates in that Work Order are applied to one in-memory complete Store snapshot. The complete deterministic successor-MAP bytes must first be written under a governed SCR candidate identity, closed successfully, reopened, and fully validated while still an SCR candidate. Only a complete validated candidate may be promoted by host rename into one new immutable MAP artifact.

The inherited MAP remains unchanged. The successful SCR-to-MAP rename is the Store-state commit point. A failed run must not create a valid successor MAP; a malformed, incomplete, or unpromoted MAP candidate remains visible non-authoritative SCR evidence rather than Store state.

RID reconstruction/replacement is not a WASM-002 Store-mutation path.

P2-03 successor publication precondition: before any final RID/COL/MAP promotion for a successor Store-state transaction, Data Sculptor identifies the lineage's chronology predecessor and establishes one truthful observed host transaction UTC. For an existing lineage, that UTC must be strictly greater than the current structurally valid Store MAP UTC, regardless of whether the Work Order's base MAP is current or historical. Equal or earlier observed UTC refuses publication; no artificial +1 ms, sleep-and-retry loop, UUID tie-break, older-predecessor fallback, or branch chronology is permitted. The chronology predecessor remains current and unchanged.

Future-dated current Store MAP: a structurally valid current MAP with a governed UTC later than truthful observed host UTC is a clock-order conflict, not by itself Store corruption. It remains current and successor publication is blocked. Help must identify the exact blocking MAP and explain the analyst-owned exits: correct an incorrect host clock; wait/rerun after truthful time advances beyond the predecessor; or deliberately move that exact future-dated current Store MAP out of the active Suitcase root and reopen/rescan. Moving it is an analyst filesystem action, not a governed Data Sculptor mutation. An older structurally valid MAP may then become current; returning the future-dated MAP may restore its authority under the ordinary greatest-UTC rule.

F-13 single-writer pre-commit guard: immediately before the final successor Store-MAP promotion, Data Sculptor re-resolves the relevant current Store authority and exact-source routing state on which the transaction depended. For an existing lineage, the current chronology predecessor must still be the authority against which the transaction was prepared; for a new-Store transaction, no newly established routable lineage may have appeared that changes the routing decision. If relevant governed state changed while the transaction was in flight, publication refuses. Data Sculptor must not overwrite the newer authority, silently rebase onto it, create a competing branch, or report success. Any RID/COL/candidate artifacts already produced are handled by the existing rollback / attributable recovery-evidence rules and do not become committed Store membership without the final valid MAP binding.

F-21 historical-base publication rule: when the applicable Store-state base is a valid historical MAP rather than the pre-run current MAP, the complete successor snapshot is still derived from that explicitly selected base plus the current Work Order's requested changes. Publication does not silently merge later state from the formerly current MAP back into the successor. Therefore mappings or aliases introduced only after the selected historical base may be absent from the new successor when the requested operation does not recreate them. That is the deliberate consequence of using the historical base, not data loss caused by an implicit merge.

The pre-run current MAP remains the chronology predecessor solely for monotonic publication ordering and stale-authority protection. Successful publication leaves both the historical base and the formerly current MAP byte-for-byte unchanged, publishes one new immutable successor MAP in the same lineage, and makes that successor current under the ordinary chronology rule. No branch identifier, hidden branch state, overwrite, in-place rollback, or automatic rebase is created.

W002-STOR-019.6

Store MAP CSV schema is exactly eight columns

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical WASM-002 Store MAP is a CSV whose header row is exactly:

store_alias,rid_filename,rid_alias,source_filename,source_column_number,source_header,alias,column_filename

Each data row describes one current logical materialized-column mapping:

  • store_alias — current human-facing Store name;
  • rid_filename — exact immutable governed RID artifact filename that physically anchors this Store lineage;
  • rid_alias — current human-facing RID name;
  • source_filename — exact visible source filename common to every row in this one-Store MAP and therefore the Store source identity;
  • source_column_number — 1-based source-column ordinal;
  • source_header — exact decoded CSV header value after governed parsing;
  • alias — current human-facing COL name; and
  • column_filename — exact physical governed COL artifact filename represented by the row.

Every row in one valid Store MAP must carry the same exact rid_filename and the same exact source_filename. A MAP that mixes RID lineages or source filenames is invalid. The logical source-column key for COL alias continuity remains the exact triple (source_filename, source_column_number, source_header). The Store is physically identified by the repeated exact rid_filename, not by mutable aliases.

F-05/P2-01 reconciliation: the superseded redundant Store-source column is removed. One Store MAP represents exactly one Store lineage and exactly one source identity, so the common source_filename supplies the required source identity without a second Store-source field.

P3-06 identity-evidence boundary: this eight-column MAP profile intentionally records governed physical filenames and mapping metadata, not per-artifact byte lengths, row counts, digests, or historical-content fingerprints. A MAP therefore cannot prove that a same-named RID or COL restored later is byte-for-byte identical to the earlier artifact. WASM-002 must not make that claim unless separate authoritative fingerprint evidence exists outside this MAP profile.

P2-04 schema consequence: no byte-length, RID-N, digest, or per-artifact fingerprint columns are added to the eight-column Store MAP to close restoration validation. The MAP remains compact relationship/state metadata. Stronger byte-identity assurance remains the responsibility of explicit fingerprint evidence outside ordinary WASM-002 Store governance.

W002-STOR-019.7

Source headers become default COL aliases on first materialization

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

When a logical source column is materialized and its exact logical key does not already exist in the inherited Store MAP, its default COL alias is its operational column name. For an exact decoded source_header of at most 1,024 Unicode scalar values, the operational name is that exact header text. For an exact decoded source_header longer than 1,024 scalar values, the operational name begins as Column <LETTERS> from the column's 1-based physical source ordinal (for example Column A, Column Z, Column AA, through Column XFD).

The exact source_header remains unchanged in the Store MAP and physical COL header; the operational name exists only to provide a bounded human-facing/default-alias value. HEADER selection continues to match the exact decoded source header under W002-STEPS-002.

If an oversized-header base fallback Column <LETTERS> would collide in the complete successor alias namespace, Data Sculptor deterministically tries Column <LETTERS> [<ordinal>]; if that also collides, it appends -2, -3, and so on until the first available exact value is found. This is the only automatic alias-suffix rule in WASM-002. A short exact source-header default that is empty or collides still refuses unless the Work Order supplies an explicit valid alias; Data Sculptor must not suffix or rewrite it.

If the same Work Order supplies an explicit alias for a newly materialized column, the explicit governed alias overrides the operational default and must pass the ordinary exact uniqueness/shadowing rules without automatic suffix repair.

For a previously materialized COL, RESET COL "<reference>" ALIAS restores this same deterministic operational default from the exact recorded source_header and physical source ordinal. An oversized recorded header therefore restores its deterministic fallback/disambiguated operational name rather than inserting the potentially very long exact header into the alias field. A short empty/colliding source-header default still refuses rather than inventing a substitute.

W002-STOR-019.8

Ordinary rematerialization preserves Store metadata, inherited RID, and inherited COL alias

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

If a newly materialized column's exact logical key already exists in the inherited Store MAP, Data Sculptor must preserve that row's current COL alias unless the Work Order explicitly changes it. The successor MAP replaces only that logical row's column_filename with the newly created physical COL artifact filename.

Ordinary rematerialization must preserve the inherited Store's exact common source_filename and rid_filename. It must not silently create a different Store, replace the Store RID, revert a user-facing Store/RID alias, or revert a COL alias to its source header. Every row in the successor MAP continues to carry that same common Store source_filename.

WASM-002 has no executable operation that replaces rid_filename while preserving the same Store lineage. A different RID filename therefore cannot be introduced as ordinary successor-state continuity in this build.

W002-STOR-019.9

Store MAP serialization is deterministic UTF-8 CSV

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Store MAP CSV files are encoded as UTF-8 without BOM and use LF (0x0A) record termination. The exact eight-field header in W002-STOR-019.6 is written once as the first row. Fields use standard CSV quoting semantics: a field containing comma, double quote, CR, or LF is enclosed in double quotes, and embedded double quotes are doubled. No locale-dependent formatting is permitted.

Every data row in one MAP must contain byte-for-byte identical values for store_alias, rid_filename, rid_alias, and source_filename. Mapping rows are written deterministically by ascending numeric source_column_number, then ascending UTF-8 byte order of source_header. Because one valid Store MAP has exactly one common source_filename, that field is not needed as a leading row-sort discriminator. Two rows with the same logical source-column key (source_filename, source_column_number, source_header) are invalid.

W002-STOR-019.10

Only a complete validated Store MAP is eligible for inheritance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A canonical MAP filename alone does not make a file a structurally valid Store MAP. For Store-MAP structural validity, the MAP artifact itself must be readable as complete UTF-8, have the exact eight-column schema, parse deterministically, satisfy Store-level consistency, lineage, deterministic row-order, mapping-key, and alias constraints, and carry structurally valid governed RID/COL filename bindings. The present health of the referenced RID/COL artifacts is a separate question and does not determine whether the MAP itself is structurally valid.

A Store MAP remains part of governed Store history when its own bytes, schema, lineage facts, and deterministic structural rules are valid even if a referenced RID or COL later becomes missing or invalid. Referenced-artifact damage therefore does not make the current structurally valid Store MAP disappear and does not by itself cause fallback to an older MAP.

F-03 current Store MAP selection

Current-state selection is performed independently within one exact Store lineage. Only structurally valid Store MAP artifacts participate. Among those MAPs, the ordinary frozen chronology rule selects the unique structurally valid MAP with the greatest canonical UTC millisecond timestamp.

  • A structurally malformed newer MAP is never current.
  • If a newer canonical MAP artifact is structurally malformed, Data Sculptor uses the greatest earlier structurally valid Store MAP in that same lineage, if one exists, and reports the malformed newer artifact through governed Help/evidence surfaces.
  • This fallback applies to structural MAP invalidity only. It does not apply merely because a structurally valid current MAP references a damaged RID or COL.
  • If two or more structurally valid MAPs share the greatest canonical UTC millisecond timestamp, current authority is ambiguous and selection refuses rather than breaking the tie by UUID, discovery order, directory order, or filesystem modified time.

P3-07 routing distinction: Store-MAP inheritance eligibility is stricter than lineage discovery. A Store lineage participates in exact-SOURCE routing when at least one Store MAP in that lineage is structurally valid, even if the current Store later evaluates DEGRADED or INVALID. Referenced RID/COL health is evaluated after routing and may cause refusal; it must not make an already discoverable lineage disappear.

For successor publication, after the required RID/COL physical promotions have succeeded, Data Sculptor uses the already-established publication-transaction UTC and allocates a MAP-specific UUID before opening the complete deterministic MAP CSV under its governed SCR candidate identity. The SCR filename therefore already carries the exact UTC, UUID, and .csv extension intended for the final MAP identity. The candidate is closed successfully, reopened, and validated for bytes, schema, Store-level consistency, aliases, RID binding, COL bindings, deterministic row order, and all other MAP eligibility rules while it remains SCR.

Only after that validation succeeds may Data Sculptor promote the candidate by host rename that changes only the three-letter semantic class token from SCR to MAP. The candidate bytes, UTC, UUID, and extension must remain unchanged across promotion. The successful rename is the publication/commit point. If validation or rename fails, no successor MAP becomes eligible/current; the candidate remains or is retained as visible non-authoritative SCR evidence. Store-aware automatic selection therefore continues to use the greatest earlier valid MAP in the same Store lineage, if one exists, while Help reports the failed candidate/publication rather than silently treating it as current state.

P3-06 governed artifact-validation tiers. Store-health status and full content validity are distinct assurances. The following two tiers are normative for WASM-002:

  • Tier 1 — Store-health structural validation. Used for routine Store status, source routing, historical-MAP health gates, inheritance decisions that do not consume analytical artifact contents, and alias-only maintenance. The selected Store MAP itself is fully parsed and structurally validated because it is the compact authority for the snapshot. A referenced RID passes Tier 1 only when the exact MAP-bound governed RID filename is present and readable, the bytes begin with exactly one UTF-8 BOM, the first logical record is a canonical N=<value> header, the final byte is LF, and the physical byte length equals the deterministic length implied by the canonical RID representation for that declared N. Tier 1 does not rescan every RID data record merely to perform routine status or alias work. A referenced COL passes Tier 1 only when the exact MAP-bound governed COL filename is present and readable, begins with exactly one UTF-8 BOM, exposes the canonical one-column CSV header whose decoded value exactly equals the MAP row's recorded source_header, and ends with LF. Tier 1 does not stream every COL value merely to establish routine Store health.
  • Tier 2 — full artifact validation. Used whenever an operation actually consumes RID/COL contents, for complete validation of newly created candidates before commit, and by REPAIR MAP after the repair operation has been validly entered. A RID passes Tier 2 only when a full stream proves the canonical N=<value> header, exactly N data records, and exact ordered values 1..N. A COL passes Tier 2 only when a full stream proves canonical one-column CSV encoding/serialization, the exact expected header, and exactly N logical data records aligned to the Store RID.

VALID, DEGRADED, and INVALID are Store-health states evaluated from the governed current snapshot using the required validation tier; they are not claims of cryptographic historical identity. When REPAIR MAP is validly invoked, it must perform Tier 2 validation of the RID and every mapped COL that would survive into the successor. The deterministic repair result removes exactly the mapped COL bindings that fail that Tier 2 check, subject to the separately frozen refusal when no mapped COL would remain. Two implementations presented with the same bytes must therefore identify the same repair set.

External restoration boundary: a file placed back under an original governed RID/COL physical filename may re-enter use only when it passes the validation tier required by the operation. Filename equality plus governed validation is sufficient for operation eligibility under this WASM-002 boundary; it is not proof that the restored bytes are the historical original bytes. Stronger historical-byte identity requires separate authoritative fingerprint evidence.

P3-10 terminology boundary: Store-state repair is REPAIR MAP. Work Order alias-registry repair is REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY. These are distinct governed operations and the integrated specification must not describe a Store REPAIR MAP Work Order as a “registry-repair Work Order.” This corrects wording only; it does not change either operation's frozen semantics.

F-08 / F-03 REPAIR MAP Work Order structure and target precondition:

SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS "Repair Crime Store"
MAP "__DS__MAP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv"
REPAIR MAP

Exactly one MAP "<filename>" clause is mandatory. It names the exact physical filename of one structurally valid Store MAP. At Run time, that named MAP must be the current structurally valid Store MAP for exactly one lineage and the target Store must currently evaluate DEGRADED. A historical Store MAP, WKO MAP, missing MAP, malformed MAP, ambiguous equal-latest current state, MAP from an unsupported profile, or target Store that does not evaluate DEGRADED refuses.

No SOURCE, Store/RID/COL alias selector or mutation, KEEP, materialization, conversion, Inventory, registry repair, cataloging, or composition clause is supplied in the same WKO. The analyst selects the Store by exact current Store MAP identity; Data Sculptor determines which mapped non-RID COL bindings are broken. The terminal DS-STEPS clause is REPAIR MAP; the Receipt operation token is separately REPAIR_MAP.

P2-03 monotonic eligibility boundary: structural validity/eligibility and chronology are separate. A structurally valid future-dated Store MAP remains a structurally valid MAP and participates in current-state selection. It is not demoted merely because the host clock is presently earlier. The monotonic guard applies when publishing a successor: truthful observed transaction UTC must be strictly greater than the chronology predecessor UTC before any successor state may commit.

P2-04 closure — validation depth is now complete. The Tier-1/Tier-2 rules in this requirement are the complete WASM-002 oracle for deciding whether a MAP-bound RID/COL is sufficiently valid for the operation being attempted. Tier 1 is intentionally bounded and is used only by operations that do not consume RID/COL analytical contents. Tier 2 is a full streaming validation and is mandatory before an operation relies on RID/COL contents, for newly created candidates before commit, and for REPAIR MAP.

REPAIR MAP determinism. Once a valid REPAIR MAP operation is entered, Data Sculptor performs Tier 2 on the Store RID and on every mapped COL. The repair successor removes exactly those mapped COL bindings whose physical COL artifacts fail Tier 2, preserves exactly those that pass Tier 2, and still refuses if zero mapped COL bindings would remain. No shallower Tier-1 result may decide the repair set.

F-03 repair semantics: after target validation, Data Sculptor confirms the named MAP is current for exactly one Store lineage, confirms the referenced RID is valid, identifies every mapped non-RID COL that is missing or invalid under the required repair validation tier, preserves every valid COL binding unchanged, removes exactly the broken COL bindings from the successor candidate, preserves the exact Store lineage RID identity and remaining Store/RID metadata, validates the complete successor MAP candidate, and publishes the successor only if every repair gate succeeds. REPAIR MAP does not reread or regenerate the source CSV, rematerialize a lost COL, regenerate the RID, or edit the predecessor MAP in place.

F-03 all-COLs-broken refusal: if removing the broken bindings would leave zero COL mapping rows, REPAIR MAP refuses. No zero-COL Store MAP is introduced, no special anchor row is invented, no successor MAP is published, and the Store remains DEGRADED. The existing current structurally valid MAP and RID continue to anchor the visible lineage.

Identity boundary. Passing Tier 1 or Tier 2 proves only that the currently visible file under the exact governed filename satisfies the applicable WASM-002 validation contract. It does not prove that those bytes are historically identical to bytes previously present under that filename. Cryptographic historical-byte identity belongs to separately governed fingerprint evidence rather than ordinary Store health.

F-15 reference-bounded eligibility: Store-MAP structural validity and inheritance eligibility are determined from the MAP artifact itself plus the governed artifacts and values that the MAP explicitly binds or that its profile explicitly requires for the validation tier being applied. Unrelated Suitcase files, unrelated Store lineages, WKOs, Receipts, Inventories, CAT/HLP/CER artifacts, analyst-owned files, directory enumeration order, and unrelated-file count cannot by their mere presence or later appearance make an already-published Store MAP eligible or ineligible. Alias-shadowing validation is a successor-publication check under W002-STOR-020; it is not a continuing ambient scan that retroactively invalidates historical MAPs.

W002-STOR-019.11

The MAP-bound RID filename is the stable physical Store identity anchor in WASM-002

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

For WASM-002, Data Sculptor does not allocate a second permanent Store UUID in addition to governed RID/MAP evidence. The exact governed rid_filename created when the Store is established is the stable physical anchor used to distinguish that Store's MAP lineage from other Stores in the same Suitcase, and every ordinary successor MAP repeats it exactly.

Within any one MAP, every row must repeat the same exact current rid_filename; disagreement is invalid. Across WASM-002 successor MAPs, a different RID filename denotes a different Store row universe and must not be silently treated as same-Store continuation.

A later PRD revision may define an explicit governed recovery transition if Red5Sorcery chooses to support replacement of a damaged RID while preserving logical continuity. No such transition is executable in WASM-002.

W002-STOR-019.12

First Store MAP has deterministic Store and RID aliases

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

When the first successful materialization establishes a Store, its first Store MAP must initialize store_alias to the exact common source_filename and rid_alias to the literal RID.

Those are the deterministic Store and RID default aliases. A later alias-only Work Order may replace them with STORE AS "<alias>" and RID AS "<alias>", clear them with CLEAR STORE ALIAS / CLEAR RID ALIAS, or restore these defaults with RESET STORE ALIAS / RESET RID ALIAS under W002-WKO-012.1 through W002-WKO-012.6. None of those operations changes the common source_filename, rid_filename, RID bytes, COL bytes, or prior MAP history.

Governed Store Catalog

W002-CAT-001

CAT is the governed collection-level Store Catalog artifact

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

WASM-002 shall define CAT as a governed Data Sculptor artifact class for cataloging a collection of CSV Stores inside one active Suitcase. CAT exists to let an analyst orient across many independently governed Stores without opening every MAP individually.

The scaling invariant is: MAP governs locally; CAT orients globally. CAT is an index over governed Store state, not a replacement for MAP and not a second Store authority.

W002-CAT-002

CAT may reference many Stores while every MAP still governs exactly one Store

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A CAT may contain entries for many Store lineages in the active Suitcase. Every MAP referenced by CAT still governs exactly one Store lineage under the frozen one-Store-per-MAP rule.

CAT must not combine multiple Stores into one MAP, synthesize a shared Store state, or centralize Store semantics that remain governed independently by each Store's MAP lineage.

W002-CAT-003

CAT has one governed CSV representation and immutable snapshot identity

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The WASM-002 Store Catalog has one durable representation: UTF-8 CSV. WASM-002 shall not emit separate HTML and CSV companion CAT artifacts for one catalog snapshot.

Each successful catalog publication creates one immutable governed artifact named exactly __DS__CAT__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv. A later catalog run publishes a new CAT snapshot; earlier CAT artifacts remain visible history and are not overwritten or deleted merely because a newer snapshot exists.

For orientation, the directory may identify the newest structurally valid CAT snapshot by the canonical UTC token. If two or more structurally valid CAT artifacts share the greatest canonical UTC timestamp, the UI must not invent chronology from UUID, discovery order, or filesystem modified time; it must surface the ambiguity and may present the tied CAT artifacts together until a later governed catalog run publishes an unambiguous newer snapshot.

F-14 publication: CAT is first written as __DS__SCR__<UTC>__<UUID>.csv using the UTC/UUID intended for the final CAT. The complete candidate must close, reopen, and validate the exact five-column schema, deterministic row ordering, row count and CSV serialization before the class token may be renamed to CAT. A failed candidate remains SCR/non-authoritative and must not be selected as a catalog snapshot.

W002-CAT-004

CAT CSV schema and row order are exact and deterministic

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical CAT header row is exactly:

store_alias,source_filename,rid_filename,map_filename,store_health

Each data row describes one routable Store lineage using values derived from the authoritative current structurally valid Store MAP selected under the existing Store rules:

  • store_alias — current human-facing Store identity;
  • source_filename — the one common exact source filename carried by that Store MAP and used for Store routing;
  • rid_filename — exact immutable governed RID filename that physically identifies the Store lineage;
  • map_filename — exact current structurally valid Store MAP used to derive the row; and
  • store_health — the Store health evaluated during this CATALOG STORES run, exactly one of VALID, DEGRADED, or INVALID.

store_health is snapshot orientation metadata, not MAP health and not an independent health authority. If the Suitcase later changes, an older CAT row continues to report the health value observed when that CAT was created.

CAT rows are sorted by ascending exact UTF-8 bytes of map_filename. The header is not part of that ordering.

W002-CAT-005

CAT is reconstructible and never becomes Store authority

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

CAT shall be reconstructible from authoritative Store MAP artifacts and the governed Store-health evaluation applied when CATALOG STORES runs. CAT must never be consulted to decide Store routing, inheritance, Store health, repair eligibility, current MAP selection, RID/COL validity, or whether a new Store may be established.

If a CAT row conflicts with authoritative MAP/Store state, current governed state wins and the CAT is stale/inconsistent. A stale CAT remains an inspectable historical governed artifact but must not be treated as current Store truth.

CAT is not automatically updated by materialization, repair, alias change, or any other Store-changing operation. The analyst creates a fresh catalog explicitly by running a new CATALOG STORES Work Order; success publishes a new immutable CAT snapshot and leaves earlier CAT snapshots visible history.

W002-CAT-006

CATALOG STORES is the standalone governed Work Order operation

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical WASM-002 Work Order form is:

SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS "Catalog Stores"
CATALOG STORES

CATALOG STORES is one standalone top-level operation. It is initiated only by an explicit analyst Work Order. No materialization, repair, alias update, conversion, or other governed operation automatically creates, rewrites, or refreshes CAT.

The operation scans authoritative governed Store MAP state, evaluates each cataloged Store's current health, and publishes one CAT snapshot plus the normal canonical Receipt. It does not mutate any Store or MAP. It must not also request materialization, conversion, alias mutation, repair, Inventory, Work Order composition, or another consequential operation in the same WKO.

The canonical Receipt operation token is CATALOG_STORES.

W002-CAT-007

CATALOG STORES derives one row per routable Store lineage from authoritative MAP state

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The catalog scan shall identify every routable Store lineage using the same structurally-valid-MAP routing definition already frozen for WASM-002. For each routable lineage, Data Sculptor evaluates current Store health exactly under W002-STOR-019.2, using the current structurally valid Store MAP selected under W002-STOR-019.10 and the applicable validation tier, and records exactly one of VALID, DEGRADED, or INVALID. Catalog presence is orientation, not permission to perform another operation.

Exactly one CAT row is emitted for each routable Store lineage, derived from that lineage's authoritative current structurally valid Store MAP and the Store-health result observed during this catalog run. If the complete authoritative collection state cannot be determined unambiguously, the operation must refuse rather than publish a knowingly incomplete or guessed CAT.

CATALOG STORES is read-only with respect to all pre-existing Store, RID, COL, MAP, source, WKO, and other Suitcase artifacts. It does not repair or mutate them.

W002-CAT-008

CAT publication is all-or-refuse and historical CAT snapshots remain visible

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

After the complete deterministic CAT row set is established, publication follows the governed all-or-refuse artifact path: write the candidate under governed scratch, close and reopen it, validate its exact filename, UTF-8/LF CSV structure, exact header, deterministic row count/order, and row references, then promote the final CAT artifact. The CAT is not successfully published until final promotion succeeds.

A publication refusal leaves prior CAT snapshots and all Store/MAP state unchanged. The Receipt records whether the catalog entry count was established and whether a final CAT filename was published.

W002-CAT-UI-001

CAT and MAP discovery reuse the existing Suitcase Directory

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

WASM-002 shall reuse the existing Data Sculptor Suitcase Directory for CAT and MAP discovery and inspection. A separate CAT/MAP browser panel shall not be added.

W002-CAT-UI-002

CAT and MAP artifacts are first-ranked in the existing directory

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The newest unambiguous structurally valid CAT snapshot, or any tied newest CAT candidates when chronology is ambiguous, and all Store MAP artifacts shall be surfaced prominently at the top of the existing Suitcase Directory ahead of ordinary Suitcase files. The presentation may be pinned, grouped, or otherwise first-ranked, provided the priority is obvious and deterministic.

W002-CAT-UI-003

CAT and MAP contents are immediately viewable from the existing HTML UI

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The analyst shall be able to select a visible CAT or MAP entry and inspect its contents through the existing read-only HTML UI without first locating or opening the artifact through the operating-system file browser.

W002-CAT-UI-004

CAT/MAP prominence preserves ordinary read-only Suitcase filtering

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The Suitcase Directory may continue to provide read-only filtered views of other Suitcase files. CAT/MAP prominence must not remove, replace, or weaken the existing ability to inspect the rest of the flat Suitcase.

W002-CAT-UI-005

Directory browsing and inspection do not require a Work Order

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Browsing, sorting, UI filtering, selecting, opening, and viewing Suitcase files are read-only inspection actions and shall not require a Work Order.

W002-CAT-UI-006

Read-only directory filtering is not governed SEARCH

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Read-only UI filtering is not the same operation as governed SEARCH. Governed SEARCH, ZIP creation, metadata changes, repairs, CAT regeneration, and every other consequential state change remain subject to the applicable Work Order and Receipt discipline.

W002-CAT-UI-007

The directory cannot mutate CAT, MAP, Store, or Suitcase state

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The Suitcase Directory shall not edit, rename, delete, repair, replace, regenerate, or otherwise mutate CAT, MAP, Store, or Suitcase state through direct GUI manipulation. Consequential changes occur only through explicit governed operations or analyst-owned filesystem actions already permitted by the canonical contract.

W002-CAT-UI-008

The CAT/MAP directory view must remain practical at large collection scale

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The CAT/MAP presentation shall make collections containing dozens or hundreds of Stores practical to inspect. An analyst must be able to understand what Stores exist, which current MAP describes each Store, and which source file each Store governs without manually opening every MAP artifact through the operating-system file browser.

W002-CAT-ACC-001

CAT acceptance proves collection-scale orientation without centralizing Store authority

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Acceptance must include a MusicBrainz-scale fixture containing 177 routable CSV Store lineages, each with its own authoritative current Store MAP. One explicit analyst-run CATALOG STORES Work Order must publish exactly one CAT snapshot containing exactly 177 data rows under the frozen five-column schema store_alias,source_filename,rid_filename,map_filename,store_health and deterministic MAP-filename ordering.

The fixture must include Stores that evaluate VALID, DEGRADED, and INVALID while retaining structurally valid current MAPs, and the CAT must record the exact health observed for each Store when the catalog run occurs. The CAT must not expose a separate MAP-health field.

The existing Suitcase Directory must surface CAT and MAP artifacts ahead of ordinary files; the analyst must be able to open CAT, inspect the collection, select and view MAP artifacts, sort/filter the directory, and inspect other Suitcase files without a Work Order. No direct GUI mutation path may be exposed.

Acceptance must alter authoritative MAP/Store state after the first CAT publication and prove that the earlier CAT is neither rewritten nor automatically refreshed. It remains visible and becomes stale/inconsistent where appropriate. Only a later explicit CATALOG STORES Work Order may reconstruct the collection and publish a new immutable CAT snapshot.

The linked WASM-003 DIR behavior remains outside the WASM-002 implementation scope: later DIR requirements auto-populate human-readable CAT/MAP descriptions, but those descriptions never become authority over CAT, MAP, or Store semantics.

Alias Binding, Suitcase Validation, and Publication

W002-STOR-020

Store, RID, and COL aliases remain human-facing metadata separate from physical identity

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Aliases are governed human-facing metadata. Creating, changing, clearing, or replacing an alias must not rename or rewrite the underlying artifact. Within one Store MAP, every non-empty COL alias and the non-empty rid_alias must be unambiguous within the row-addressable artifact alias namespace under the exact Unicode scalar-value comparison rule in PB-STOR-010.

F-15 publication-time shadowing boundary: alias uniqueness and physical-name shadowing are validated when a candidate successor Store MAP is being published, against the comparison domain applicable to that one Store snapshot and the then-visible governed physical targets it makes row-addressable. If an alias would exactly collide with another addressable alias or physical filename in that publication domain, publication refuses. After a Store MAP has been validly published, the later appearance, disappearance, rename, or copying-in of an unrelated Suitcase file does not retroactively make that immutable MAP structurally invalid or ineligible. A later textual reference can still become ambiguous at resolution time under W002-STOR-021; that ambiguity causes the later operation to refuse rather than changing the historical MAP's validity.

The store_alias names the Store as a whole and is separate from the field/COL alias namespace. Alias mutation occurs through a governed Work Order, not through an editable GUI field. Exact cross-Store Store-alias uniqueness and future selection-by-Store-alias syntax remain outside this freeze.

W002-STOR-021

Work Order resolution binds one exact Store MAP and physical targets

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A saved Work Order may refer to governed materialized columns by exact physical filename or by a unique COL alias from one selected Store MAP. The canonical explicit Store-MAP selector is MAP "<exact Store MAP filename>" under W002-STOR-019.3 and W002-WKO-012.3. If that clause is present and valid, exactly that Store snapshot is used. Otherwise Data Sculptor applies the Store-aware source-qualified selection rule in W002-STOR-019.2.

All textual physical-filename and COL-alias comparisons in this resolution step use exact Unicode scalar-value sequence equality under PB-STOR-010: no case folding, Unicode normalization, trimming, locale equivalence, or filesystem enumeration heuristic is permitted. Resolution is bounded to the selected Store snapshot and the physical targets/aliases that are addressable through that snapshot. If the supplied text has no exact target, resolution refuses. If it has more than one exact possible target in that domain—for example because a currently visible physical filename and a current alias are both exact matches—resolution also refuses. Data Sculptor must not choose filename over alias, alias over filename, first-found entry, directory order, modified time, UUID, or any other tie-break heuristic.

Before execution, Data Sculptor must record the exact physical Store MAP identity when one is used, bind the run to its exact rid_filename, and resolve aliases deterministically to physical COL artifacts. The selected Store MAP must remain fixed for the run even if a newer MAP is created during that same run. This protects Store/selection continuity but does not by itself claim that bytes stored under an analyst-owned source filename are cryptographically identical across different runs.

W002-STOR-022

Each successful Suitcase validation publishes one retained governed CER HTML certificate

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A selected directory becomes a validated Suitcase only when Data Sculptor successfully creates, completely writes, and closes one governed CER HTML Suitcase Validation Certificate in that directory. The certificate itself is the validation artifact and remains visible in the flat Suitcase as durable evidence.

No validation-only delete or rename is required. Failure to create, completely write, or close the certificate means the directory has not passed Suitcase validation and analytical execution remains locked.

F-14 CER exception: the CER is deliberately not staged as SCR. Suitcase validation is specifically the direct create/write/close test of the final canonical CER identity in the selected directory. Inserting an SCR-to-CER rename would test a different publication path and is therefore forbidden for this validation step. A successful CER does not pre-certify later SCR-to-final renames for other artifact classes.

F-24 CER lifecycle: every successful explicit Suitcase selection and validation publishes exactly one fresh immutable CER with a new governed UTC+UUID identity. Data Sculptor must not satisfy a new validation event by reusing an earlier CER. Every prior valid CER remains a standalone historical artifact under its original governed filename and exact bytes.

WASM-002 performs no automatic CER deletion, replacement, compaction, or CER-history ZIP packaging. Historical CERs are not housekeeping candidates merely because a newer CER exists. Any later archival or packaging capability must be separately governed and explicitly invoked; it is not part of the WASM-002 validation lifecycle.

W002-STOR-022.1

Suitcase Validation Certificate physical identity and longest-name path gate

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The exact certificate filename is __DS__CER__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.html, using the canonical UTC millisecond token and canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID v4. Data Sculptor chooses the filename; the analyst does not supply or edit it.

The CER create/write/close test begins only after the browser host has satisfied the required user-selected writable-directory capability in W002-PLAT-001. A browser that cannot expose that capability produces a host-capability refusal before folder validation; that condition is not evidence that any particular directory is unwritable or filename-incompatible.

WASM-002 path/filename acceptance must derive the maximum filename length from every governed final-artifact filename form and every governed SCR staging form that this build can actually emit. Under the current contract, the maximum is 73 ASCII bytes/characters: the governed .html CER/HLP final forms and an SCR candidate reserved for a .html final artifact have that length. The canonical CER filename therefore exercises the current maximum emitted filename length during the create/write/close validation test.

On a supported host, successful create/write/close of this canonical governed HTML filename is the WASM-002 folder filename/path compatibility test for the current emitted-name maximum. Data Sculptor does not maintain a product-level table of operating-system numeric path maxima and must not truncate, abbreviate, hash-shorten, or otherwise mutate a governed filename to fit a host path limitation. If the certificate cannot be created under its canonical name after a directory has actually been selected through the supported-host contract, the selected directory does not pass validation.

If a future PRD revision introduces an emitted final or staging filename longer than the current CER/HLP/SCR-HTML maximum, acceptance must detect that change and explicitly exercise the new maximum before the build may rely on this path-compatibility claim.

W002-STOR-022.2

Suitcase Validation Certificate semantic content

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The HTML certificate uses the canonical built-in Data Sculptor presentation and must visibly contain, at minimum:

SUITCASE VALIDATION CERTIFICATE
RESULT: PASS
SUITCASE: .
UTC: <canonical certificate UTC>
UUID: <certificate UUID>
ARTIFACT: <full governed certificate filename>
TEST: CREATE_WRITE_CLOSE

It must state that Data Sculptor successfully created, completely wrote, and closed this governed HTML certificate in the selected Suitcase. It must state that this establishes that the selected directory was writable by Data Sculptor at the recorded UTC and accepted the governed artifact filename used for the certificate.

It must also state that the certificate does not certify available disk capacity, guarantee success of future analytical operations, or certify later SCR-to-final-class publication/rename operations. The semantic record uses SUITCASE: . and must not persist an absolute machine-specific path merely to prove validation.

W002-STOR-022.3

Suitcase Validation Certificate uses the canonical built-in presentation in WASM-002

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The certificate is a human-facing HTML CER artifact and uses the canonical built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor presentation in WASM-002. Presentation must never change RESULT, SUITCASE, UTC, UUID, artifact identity, TEST, validation meaning, or limitation facts.

Configurable Brand Manifest application to CER artifacts is deferred to V1-BACKLOG / a future build and is not required for WASM-002 Suitcase validation.

W002-STOR-023

Non-Store governed artifacts use class-specific all-or-refuse publication profiles

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Except for the deliberate CER Suitcase-validation path below, WASM-002 does not place a newly generated durable artifact into its final semantic class merely because candidate bytes exist. The complete candidate is first written under the governed SCR identity defined by W002-STOR-023.1, closed, reopened, and validated against the target class contract. Only a candidate that passes its class-specific publication predicate may be renamed into the intended final class. A final-class filename therefore records successful class publication, not broader authority where a separate MAP/registry relationship governs authority.

F-33 reserved-class boundary: DGN, RCV, BRD, and LCK are registered but not emitted by WASM-002, so they do not appear as publication profiles in this table and have no WASM-002 producer here.

Final classFinal serialization / identityPublication predicateAuthority boundary
WKO__DS__WKO__<UTC>__<UUID>.txtThe complete candidate obeys the saved-Work-Order lifecycle and parses completely under exactly one WASM-002 executable operation grammar with the required SUITCASE: ., exactly one non-whitespace WORK ORDER AS alias, and the governed lexical/comment rules. Applicable save-time alias/registry gates must also pass before the save transaction may commit.Promotion proves a valid immutable WKO artifact. Alias-registry authority is not committed until the complete successor WKO MAP is successfully published under W002-STOR-018.3.
RCP__DS__RCP__<UTC>__<UUID>.txtThe complete candidate validates against W002-RCP-005 through W002-RCP-008: exact deterministic TXT serialization, common envelope, applicable operation-specific key table, governed absence semantics, and created-artifact tail.Publication creates durable run evidence only. It does not retroactively create or change analytical state.
HLP__DS__HLP__<UTC>__<UUID>.htmlThe complete self-contained HTML satisfies the HLP disclosure, presentation, provenance, embedded-JSON, lineage and semantic-parity rules in W002-HELP-009 and related Help requirements.Publication creates durable Help/support evidence. It does not override the underlying diagnostic event or analytical state.
CVT__DS__CVT__<UTC>__<UUID>.csvThe bounded Windows-1252 conversion completes, the original analyst-owned source remains unchanged, the converted bytes pass the governed strict UTF-8 requirement, and the candidate closes/reopens successfully. Structural CSV interpretation remains a later certification/materialization concern.The published exact CVT filename is a new immutable governed source identity for later routing under W002-CONV-004.
INV__DS__INV__<UTC>__<UUID>.txtThe complete inventory scan has established the governed entry set and the candidate validates the deterministic INV serialization, count, metadata availability and ordering rules.Publication creates an immutable inventory snapshot; it is evidence/orientation, not Store authority.

MAP remains authoritative for each Store.
