0x9ALATIN SMALL LETTER S WITH CARONU+0161
0x9BSINGLE RIGHT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARKU+203A
0x9CLATIN SMALL LIGATURE OEU+0153
0x9DUNDEFINED—
0x9ELATIN SMALL LETTER Z WITH CARONU+017E
0x9FLATIN CAPITAL LETTER Y WITH DIAERESISU+0178

0xA0–0xFF

Every byte 0xA0 through 0xFF maps one-to-one to Unicode U+00A0 through U+00FF.

Undefined-byte rule

The only undefined byte values in this frozen WASM-002 mapping are exactly 0x81, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0x90, and 0x9D. Encountering any one of them makes the complete compatibility assessment INCOMPATIBLE at the first such byte and causes an explicitly run conversion Work Order to refuse before transcoding rather than guess.

These three ranges plus the 32-position table above exhaust the byte domain 0x00–0xFF. No unlisted byte value exists.

W002-CONV-002.5

The compatibility check must itself be bounded and deterministic.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The compatibility check is one bounded-memory deterministic sequential pass from physical source byte offset 0 to EOF unless the first undefined Windows-1252 byte is encountered earlier. Buffer/window size must not change the compatibility outcome or the first undefined-byte offset.

On INCOMPATIBLE, WINDOWS_1252_FIRST_UNDEFINED_BYTE_OFFSET is the zero-based absolute physical source-byte offset of the first undefined byte. On COMPATIBLE, that offset is NOT_APPLICABLE. If the assessment begins but an independent read/host failure prevents a governed compatibility conclusion, the outcome is NOT_AVAILABLE and the first-undefined-byte offset is NOT_AVAILABLE. The assessment itself publishes no converted output.

W002-CONV-003

Help suggestion after failed UTF-8 certification

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Help may suggest the separate CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 Work Order only when the governed engine emits DS-CNV-001 after a complete compatibility assessment returned COMPATIBLE. The suggestion is therefore derived from a governed diagnostic fact, not from the UTF-8 failure itself.

If the assessment returns INCOMPATIBLE, is NOT_AVAILABLE, or did not run, DS-CNV-001 is not emitted and Help must not invent the conversion recommendation.

P3-08 Help disclosure: when conversion succeeds, Help must state that the published CVT is a new governed source artifact with its own source identity and that converting a refreshed legacy source later will publish another distinct CVT rather than refresh an earlier CVT-backed Store lineage. When a CVT is selected for first materialization, Help must disclose the same consequence before or with the normal materialization guidance: the Store lineage is anchored to the exact CVT filename, not to the analyst-owned pre-conversion filename. Help must not imply hidden lineage continuity across separate CVT artifacts.

W002-CONV-003.1

The suggestion must state that the current analytical task has stopped.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The suggestion must state that the current analytical task has already stopped/refused because strict UTF-8 certification failed. DS-CNV-001 is informational and must not be rendered as though materialization can continue from the failed run.

W002-CONV-003.2

The suggestion must state that the original source has not been changed.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The suggestion must state that the compatibility assessment was read-only and that Data Sculptor did not change the analyst-owned source. Any later successful conversion publishes a separate governed CVT artifact rather than editing the original source in place.

W002-CONV-003.3

The suggestion must describe the source as compatible with the supported Windows-1252 converter, not definitively identified as Windows-1252.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The suggestion must describe the complete source as compatible with Data Sculptor's supported Windows-1252 converter. It must not say that the source was definitively identified as Windows-1252 or imply provenance that the compatibility pass cannot prove.

W002-CONV-003.4

The suggestion must make clear that conversion is a separate user-authorized task.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The suggestion must make clear that conversion is a separate user-authorized Work Order. next_action: RUN_WINDOWS_1252_CONVERSION means that the separate operation is a governed safe option; it is not permission for Data Sculptor to silently transcode, modify the source, or reinterpret the refused analytical Work Order.

W002-CONV-003.5

If the bytes are not compatible with the supported converter, Help must not recommend Windows-1252 conversion as though it were safe.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

If the compatibility outcome is INCOMPATIBLE, NOT_AVAILABLE, or NOT_RUN, Help must not recommend Windows-1252 conversion as though it were safe. In particular, the mere presence of DS-ENC-001 never authorizes that recommendation.

W002-CONV-004

Canonical conversion output

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A successful Windows-1252 conversion task must produce canonical UTF-8 output suitable for later submission to the normal UTF-8 certification and materialization path.

P3-08 lineage consequence: the successful conversion output is a new immutable governed CVT artifact with its own exact physical filename. That CVT filename is the source identity used by later Store routing. A later conversion, including one made from a refreshed analyst-owned legacy source with the same original filename, publishes a different CVT and therefore does not refresh, replace, or continue an earlier CVT-backed Store lineage merely by name association. On first materialization, each distinct CVT begins a new Store lineage unless that exact CVT filename already routes to an existing lineage under the normal Store rules.

F-14 CVT identity and publication: the final converted-source filename is exactly __DS__CVT__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv. Conversion writes first to the corresponding W002-STOR-023.1 SCR identity with the same UTC, UUID and .csv extension. Only after bounded conversion completes, the candidate closes/reopens successfully, and the converted bytes satisfy the governed strict UTF-8 requirement may the class token be renamed to CVT. CSV structural interpretation remains governed by the later normal certification/materialization path; CVT publication does not assert that the converted source is structurally valid CSV.

F-10 conversion semantics — encoding conversion only

The conversion operation performs deterministic character transcoding only. It does not parse, repair, normalize, or reinterpret CSV structure.

  • Commas remain commas.
  • Double quotes remain double quotes.
  • Ordinary ASCII bytes retain the same byte value.
  • LF remains LF.
  • CR remains CR.
  • CRLF remains CRLF.
  • Embedded CR/LF bytes are preserved in place; the converter does not decide whether they are record terminators or field content.

Canonical UTF-8 output therefore means deterministic UTF-8 encoding of the accepted source characters, not normalization of line endings, quoting, delimiters, records, headers, or fields.

F-10 BOM rule

  • The published CVT is UTF-8 without a BOM; Data Sculptor does not prepend EF BB BF.
  • If the source failed strict UTF-8 classification, a leading source byte sequence EF BB BF is not blindly stripped as though it were a UTF-8 BOM. Under the Windows-1252 conversion path those source bytes are source data and are mapped according to the frozen Windows-1252 mapping.
  • BOM interpretation remains subordinate to encoding classification rather than acting as a blind prefix-removal rule.
W002-CONV-004.1

The converted artifact must itself be certifiable as UTF-8.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-CONV-004.2

The conversion Receipt identifies the governed source encoding

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical RCP for a successful governed Windows-1252-compatible conversion must identify exactly SOURCE_ENCODING: WINDOWS-1252-COMPATIBLE.

That operation-specific fact is carried within the canonical TXT Receipt governed by W002-RCP-001 through W002-RCP-010. Only that exact serialized spelling is permitted for this key/value pair.

W002-CONV-004.3

The conversion Receipt identifies the materialized UTF-8 encoding

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical RCP for a successful governed conversion must identify exactly MATERIALIZED_ENCODING: UTF-8.

This uses the canonical KEY: VALUE serialization frozen by W002-RCP-005. MATERIALIZED_ENCODING=UTF-8 is not valid canonical Receipt serialization.

W002-CONV-004.4

The conversion Receipt identifies bounded streaming transcoding

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical RCP for successful conversion must identify that transcoding was performed under the governed bounded/streaming conversion contract.

W002-CONV-004.5

No analytical column materialization occurs as part of this conversion operation.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Help Engine — First-Class Product Surface

Design rationale — why Help is part of the workspace

Rationale, not independent scope authority. The numbered W002-HELP-* and W002-UI-* requirements below govern. This discussion records the problem those requirements are intended to solve so later implementation does not preserve the words while losing the design purpose.

The operational problem is lossy problem reporting. Conventional analytical software often turns a refusal into a transient dialog, screenshot, copied error string, or half-remembered paraphrase. By the time the problem reaches IT or another analyst, the original execution phase, exact evidence, offsets, Work Order context, and boundary facts may be missing. Data Sculptor should preserve the diagnostic record instead of asking a human to reconstruct it.

The live Help pane and the saved Help report are renderings, not truth. The canonical diagnostic event emitted by the governed engine is authoritative. The browser Help / Diagnostic Surface is a transient projection of that event inside the working context. The saved HTML Help Report is a durable projection of the same event for retention and handoff. Neither UI state nor prose may override, repair, soften, or invent the underlying diagnostic facts.

Co-presence prevents modal amnesia. A governed refusal should remain visible beside the Work Order, execution stages, source/Suitcase context, and generated artifacts that explain how the user arrived there. Application-controlled modal dialogs that hide those surfaces would sever the cognitive link between intent, observed evidence, refusal, and safe next action. The dedicated Help / Diagnostic Surface therefore occupies persistent workspace real estate rather than appearing only as a transient popup.

Different voice, same truth. Casual, Office Speak, and Technical renderings may vary vocabulary, sentence structure, notation, pedagogical depth, and how much supporting explanation they show. They may not change the canonical diagnostic identity, severity, evidence, refusal/continue decision, provenance, or safe next action. A voice may format the same byte offset differently; it may not replace exact evidence with a weaker claim.

WASM-002 proves the wiring, not the finished prose library. The governed engine emits a stable diagnostic ID plus structured facts. The Help layer resolves that ID through one validated catalog containing Casual, Office Speak, and Technical templates. The development source is help_messages.json; the build validates it and embeds the validated catalog directly into the released Data Sculptor HTML, so runtime Help does not depend on a network request or adjacent catalog file. During WASM-002 the catalog may use unmistakable mechanically generated placeholder text whose purpose is to prove lookup, interpolation, switching, coverage, and semantic parity. The complete authored Help corpus is a later content milestone and must not become a prerequisite for accepting the WASM-002 execution architecture.

The saved report is a support-handoff artifact. The user must be able to create a styled, self-contained HTML document that stands on its own outside Data Sculptor and can be retained in the Suitcase, attached to an IT ticket, emailed to another analyst, or opened on an offline workstation. The report is designed for two audiences in one file: a readable explanation for the analyst or manager and a structured facts section for technical staff. When relevant, it records the canonical execution-boundary facts source_modified_by_data_sculptor, materialization_started, analytical_outputs_published, and store_state_committed directly from governed execution state.

Self-contained does not mean pixel-identical or immutable. The report must have no runtime dependency on Data Sculptor, a network connection, remote fonts, external stylesheets, or any external presentation resource. System font substitution and ordinary browser differences are acceptable so long as meaning, hierarchy, evidence, and accessibility are preserved. An HTML file on disk can be edited by a person. WASM-002 therefore gives the HLP an immutable governed identity and explicit lineage but does not automatically SHA-256 the report or create/refresh an LCK. The final HLP bytes remain eligible for exact-byte evidence later through the explicit FINGERPRINT/LCK workflow.

Support handoff must not become a data-egress path. WASM-002 uses a fixed disclosure allowlist rather than generating broad context and attempting to redact it afterward. A Help Report may carry the exact source filename, relevant column/header/ordinal and bounded execution evidence, governed artifact filenames, and only the minimum executable Work Order clause(s) needed to explain the diagnostic. It does not automatically include source rows or values, absolute local paths, unrelated columns, the complete Work Order, Work Order comments, unrelated Suitcase contents, browser/environment internals, or raw ungoverned stack traces. Every HLP visibly states the disclosure boundary it applied.

ComponentNatureRole and authority
Canonical Diagnostic EventShared-core governed stateAuthoritative truth. Stable diagnostic identity plus structured facts, evidence, severity/classification, execution decision, provenance, and safe next action.
Help / Diagnostic SurfaceTransient workspace projectionImmediate explanation. Persistent co-present viewport into the event; supports voice switching and remediation without becoming a second source of truth.
HTML Help ReportDurable Suitcase artifactPortable evidence / support handoff. Self-contained human-readable explanation and structured technical facts rendered from the same canonical event.
W002-HELP-001

Canonical diagnostic truth

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Every governed user-visible failure or warning produced by WASM-002 must originate as a canonical diagnostic event. A diagnostic event must have a stable identity and structured facts independent of its final wording.

Governed success/status events that participate in the Help/status/evidence system—such as a successfully saved Work Order or a successfully validated Suitcase—are canonical INFO diagnostic events and obey the same identity/fact/behavior contract. Ordinary static labels, headings, decorative copy, and presentation-only status text are not automatically diagnostics merely because they are visible in the UI.

W002-HELP-001.1

Canonical diagnostic IDs use the frozen DS-<DOMAIN>-<NNN> grammar

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Every canonical diagnostic event must carry one stable identifier using the exact form DS-<DOMAIN>-<NNN>.

DOMAIN is exactly three uppercase ASCII letters A through Z. NNN is exactly three decimal digits, zero-padded, in the range 001 through 999. Examples include DS-ENC-001, DS-WKO-001, DS-STO-001, DS-MAT-001, and DS-HLP-001.

A diagnostic ID is permanent after allocation and must never be reused for a different diagnostic meaning. Severity, host, build/release, source filename, path, UUID, byte offset, row/column number, count, timestamp, occurrence ID, and other run-specific facts must not be encoded into the diagnostic ID; those values belong in structured diagnostic fields. The identifier is the canonical lookup key used by the Help message catalog.

Day 060 H-04 pre-freeze identifier normalization: the Windows-1252 compatibility suggestion diagnostic is DS-CNV-001. It follows the same exact three-letter DOMAIN grammar as every other diagnostic ID. No four-letter DOMAIN exception exists in the current WASM-002 contract. Any pre-H-04 draft spelling of this diagnostic is superseded and is not valid build-registry input.

W002-HELP-001.2

Diagnostic severity uses one exact token set

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Every canonical diagnostic event must carry exactly one severity token: INFO, WARNING, or ERROR.

Severity classifies the condition for human and machine interpretation. It does not itself determine whether execution continues or refuses; that authority is carried separately by the canonical behavior field.

W002-HELP-001.3

Diagnostic phase uses a stable uppercase token

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Every canonical diagnostic event must identify the governed operation or phase using an uppercase ASCII snake-case token matching [A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:_[A-Z0-9]+)*.

Examples include WORK_ORDER_VALIDATION, SOURCE_CERTIFICATION, MATERIALIZATION, STORE_PUBLICATION, and HELP_REPORT. These examples do not constitute a closed global phase list; the fixed phase for each allocated diagnostic is declared by that diagnostic's registry entry.

W002-HELP-001.4

Structured diagnostic facts are declared per diagnostic

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical event carries diagnostic-specific evidence in a structured facts object. Fact keys use lowercase ASCII snake case matching [a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+)*.

Each diagnostic registry entry declares disjoint required_facts and optional_facts sets. Every required fact must be present when that diagnostic is emitted. An optional fact key may be omitted when that fact is not emitted for the event, but omission itself has no governed absence-state meaning: it must not be interpreted as NONE, NOT_RUN, NOT_AVAILABLE, NOT_APPLICABLE, false, zero, or an empty string. An emitted fact key that is not declared for that diagnostic is invalid.

For structured JSON diagnostic facts, an established ordinary value retains its native JSON type. When a present diagnostic fact must express one of the shared governed absence states, its value is the exact JSON string "NONE", "NOT_RUN", "NOT_AVAILABLE", or "NOT_APPLICABLE", with the meaning frozen by F-18. JSON null is not a generic encoding for diagnostic-fact absence; it is permitted only where a specific JSON schema explicitly declares a nullable field and defines what that null means, as W002-HELP-009 does for HLP lineage.

A required diagnostic fact may not be silently omitted, defaulted, converted to null, guessed, or replaced by a Help-layer value. If Data Sculptor attempts to establish a registered diagnostic but cannot produce one or more facts declared required for that diagnostic, the intended diagnostic is not emitted. Instead the engine emits DS-HLP-001 under W002-HELP-001.8. The replacement event records the intended diagnostic ID and the complete sorted set of missing required fact names. No partially populated copy of the intended diagnostic may be presented beside it.

This fail-closed substitution is a diagnostic-contract integrity rule, not a presentation fallback. It preserves the F-17 boundary that diagnostics own facts and Help renders only complete governed diagnostic truth.

W002-HELP-001.5

Execution behavior is explicitly CONTINUE or REFUSE

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Every canonical diagnostic event must carry exactly one execution-behavior token: CONTINUE or REFUSE.

This field is the governed continue/refuse decision for the event. Help wording, severity, UI color, or presentation must not independently weaken, strengthen, or reinterpret it.

W002-HELP-001.6

Safe next action uses a stable token rather than Help prose

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Every canonical diagnostic event must carry a next_action token using uppercase ASCII snake case matching [A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:_[A-Z0-9]+)*. NONE is the canonical value when no safe governed next action applies.

The token expresses stable machine-readable intent; Casual, Office Speak, and Technical wording for that action belongs to the Help layer. Run-specific values such as timestamps, paths, UUIDs, byte offsets, filenames, counts, or occurrence IDs remain structured facts and do not change the diagnostic identity or fixed next-action meaning.

Damaged-Store guidance is part of the safe-next-action contract. When ordinary materialization refuses because exact source routing identifies an INVALID Store lineage, or a DEGRADED lineage whose every mapped COL is broken and therefore cannot be reduced to a non-empty successor by REPAIR MAP, the selected Help voice must preserve the same frozen choices and consequences rather than inventing a recovery operation. The explanation must identify the blocked lineage/current MAP and distinguish: external restoration under the original governed physical filename followed by the required governed validation tier; source rename to deliberately begin a separate new Store lineage; and analyst retirement of the damaged lineage by moving all of that lineage's Store MAPs out of the active Suitcase root. For retirement, Help must warn that moving only the latest MAP can expose an older structurally valid MAP as current. Help must not claim that matching the original filename proves historical byte identity, and must not describe any of these analyst filesystem actions as Data Sculptor-authored repair, deletion, RID regeneration, or silent lineage replacement.

P3-07 malformed-MAP routing guard: when ordinary materialization refuses because no routable Store lineage can be established while one or more structurally malformed Store-MAP-class artifacts are present in the active Suitcase, Help must identify the malformed MAP artifact or artifacts and state that new-Store/RID creation was blocked to prevent a silent lineage fork. Help must not describe the missing structurally valid MAP as proof that the prior Store never existed, and must not invent a Data Sculptor repair or replacement operation for this condition.

P3-10 delimiter-hint clarification: when Stage 2 refuses with INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTE and the offending byte is semicolon (0x3B) or horizontal TAB (0x09), Help may include the governed delimiter-mismatch hint even though the refusal occurred before header-delimiter resolution. The hint is explanatory only: it must not change the canonical refusal condition, location facts, behavior, or safe-action boundary.

F-16 conversion-suggestion boundary: strict UTF-8 refusal diagnostic DS-ENC-001 has fixed next_action: NONE. UTF-8 failure alone does not establish that any converter is safe. Only the separate compatibility diagnostic DS-CNV-001, emitted after the complete governed Windows-1252 compatibility assessment returns COMPATIBLE, may carry next_action: RUN_WINDOWS_1252_CONVERSION. That token identifies a safe separately authorized option; it never resumes or rewrites the refused analytical Work Order.

Day 060 H-12 damaged-lineage diagnostic binding

  • ordinary MATERIALIZE refusal for a routed INVALID Store uses DS-MAT-014 and its declared facts;
  • ordinary MATERIALIZE refusal for a DEGRADED Store whose every mapped COL is broken uses DS-MAT-015 and its declared facts;
  • the no-routable-lineage / malformed-Store-MAP guard uses DS-MAT-016 and its declared facts.

These specialized allocations are what permit closed-world Help to identify the blocked lineage/current MAP or malformed MAP artifacts without adding unrelated facts to the ordinary DS-MAT-010 validation diagnostic.

Day 060 H-26 / BM-09 ordinary DEGRADED routing binding. When ordinary MATERIALIZE exact-source routing identifies a DEGRADED Store whose RID is valid and at least one mapped non-RID COL remains valid, the refusal uses DS-MAT-017. Its fixed next_action is RUN_REPAIR_MAP because REPAIR MAP is the safe governed Store mutation for this repairable DEGRADED state. Help must use the diagnostic's declared current_map_filename as the exact MAP identity the analyst must name in the separate governed REPAIR MAP Work Order. The token does not run repair automatically and does not mutate the refused MATERIALIZE Work Order.

W002-HELP-001.7

The governed engine emits the diagnostic semantic core, not voice-authored prose

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The shared Rust/WASM diagnostic path must provide the canonical semantic core required by Help: diagnostic_id, severity, phase, behavior, facts, and next_action. The fixed values and permitted fact-key sets for an allocated diagnostic are governed by diagnostics.json.

Casual, Office Speak, and Technical prose belongs to the Help rendering layer rather than being duplicated as authored message sets inside the governed engine. Host/build/occurrence metadata may be carried by surrounding governed execution evidence, but it must not redefine the diagnostic semantic core.

F-16 closed-world Help rule: Help may recommend the WASM-002 Windows-1252 conversion Work Order only when the governed engine emitted DS-CNV-001. Help must not infer compatibility from DS-ENC-001, byte appearance, file extension, locale, browser behavior, heuristic encoding detection, or prose outside the diagnostic facts.

W002-HELP-001.8

diagnostics.json is the canonical WASM-002 diagnostic registry build resource

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The human-inspectable development/build source for the WASM-002 diagnostic registry is exactly diagnostics.json, encoded as UTF-8 without BOM. It is Data Sculptor product/build content, not a Suitcase artifact; it must not use the __DS__ namespace, consume an artifact-class token, or be copied into an analyst's Suitcase merely because Data Sculptor runs.

The top-level JSON object has exactly two fields: registry_version and diagnostics. registry_version is the string "1". diagnostics is an array written in ascending UTF-8 byte order of diagnostic_id.

Each diagnostic entry has exactly seven fields: diagnostic_id, severity, phase, behavior, next_action, required_facts, and optional_facts. Diagnostic IDs must be unique and satisfy W002-HELP-001.1. Severity, phase, behavior, and next-action values must satisfy W002-HELP-001.2 through W002-HELP-001.6. required_facts and optional_facts are arrays of canonical fact-key strings sorted in ascending UTF-8 byte order; keys must be unique within each array and the two arrays must be disjoint.

{
  "registry_version": "1",
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "diagnostic_id": "DS-CNV-001",
      "severity": "INFO",
      "phase": "SOURCE_CERTIFICATION",
      "behavior": "CONTINUE",
      "next_action": "RUN_WINDOWS_1252_CONVERSION",
      "required_facts": ["source_filename", "windows_1252_compatibility_outcome"],
      "optional_facts": []
    },
    {
      "diagnostic_id": "DS-ENC-001",
      "severity": "ERROR",
      "phase": "SOURCE_CERTIFICATION",
      "behavior": "REFUSE",
      "next_action": "NONE",
      "required_facts": ["first_invalid_byte_offset", "source_filename", "stop_reason"],
      "optional_facts": ["analytical_outputs_published", "materialization_started", "source_modified_by_data_sculptor", "store_state_committed"]
    },
    {
      "diagnostic_id": "DS-HLP-001",
      "severity": "ERROR",
      "phase": "DIAGNOSTIC_ASSEMBLY",
      "behavior": "REFUSE",
      "next_action": "NONE",
      "required_facts": ["intended_diagnostic_id", "missing_required_facts"],
      "optional_facts": []
    }
  ]
}

The PRD does not need to enumerate every allocated WASM-002 diagnostic row. The complete registry delivered with the build is retained acceptance evidence. A diagnostic ID becomes permanent once allocated and must not later be reused for a different meaning.

Build validation must fail on malformed JSON; extra/missing entry fields; duplicate or noncanonical diagnostic IDs; invalid fixed tokens; unsorted, duplicate, overlapping, or invalid fact-key declarations; engine diagnostic definitions whose fixed semantics disagree with the registry; engine diagnostic definitions absent from the registry; Help-catalog IDs absent from the registry; or Help placeholders that name facts not declared as required or optional by the matching diagnostic.

F-07 DS-ENC-001 fact mapping: the canonical lower-case diagnostic facts for strict UTF-8 refusal are first_invalid_byte_offset, source_filename, and stop_reason. For this diagnostic, stop_reason is exactly INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE. The generic fact name byte_offset is retired for this UTF-8 refusal diagnostic.

P2-03 clock-order diagnostic facts: whichever stable WASM-002 Diagnostic ID is allocated to refusal because a successor Store MAP or WKO MAP cannot satisfy the strict monotonic UTC publication guard must declare these exact lower-case required facts in its diagnostic-registry entry: map_profile, observed_host_utc, predecessor_map_filename, and predecessor_utc. map_profile has exactly two permitted values: STORE for a Store-MAP chronology guard and WKO for a Work-Order-registry-MAP chronology guard. These facts identify both the governed MAP profile, the blocking predecessor artifact, and the truthful clock observation that caused refusal.

F-16 DS-CNV-001 allocation: DS-CNV-001 is emitted only when the complete read-only compatibility assessment under W002-CONV-002 through W002-CONV-002.5 reaches EOF with outcome COMPATIBLE. Its required fact windows_1252_compatibility_outcome is therefore exactly the JSON string "COMPATIBLE". behavior: CONTINUE means this informational diagnostic introduces no additional refusal; it does not reverse the already-established DS-ENC-001 refusal or resume Stage 2.

F-17 DS-HLP-001 allocation: DS-HLP-001 is the canonical fail-safe event when the engine cannot satisfy the complete required-fact contract of an intended registered diagnostic. intended_diagnostic_id is the exact canonical ID that was being assembled. missing_required_facts is a JSON array of every missing required fact-key string, sorted in ascending UTF-8 byte order with no duplicates. The intended diagnostic is suppressed rather than emitted incompletely. DS-HLP-001 always refuses and has next_action: NONE.

F-22 QA-independence boundary: diagnostics.json is authoritative for the fixed semantic contract of an allocated Diagnostic ID — its ID, severity, phase, behavior, next action, and permitted required/optional fact keys — but the implementation-delivered registry is not, by itself, an independent oracle proving that every arbitrary runtime condition was mapped to the correct Diagnostic ID. WASM-002 does not require a second QA-owned registry duplicating every implementation allocation.

Where this PRD independently freezes a condition-to-diagnostic mapping or exact required facts — including the named DS-ENC-001, DS-CNV-001, and DS-HLP-001 contracts and other explicitly pinned diagnostic facts — that PRD text remains normative and acceptance must test the mapping independently of the implementation registry. For allocations not independently pinned by the PRD, WASM-002 accepts the validated build registry as the build allocation while retaining all registry-shape, permanence, semantic-agreement, fact-discipline, and Help cross-validation gates. This is an explicit accepted QA-scope risk, not a claim of independent condition-to-ID verification.

The required map_profile fact tells closed-world Help which governed MAP profile encountered the chronology guard: STORE means Store MAP and WKO means Work Order registry MAP. Help must select profile-appropriate explanation and analyst exits only from that declared fact and the other registered event facts; it must not infer the profile from filename shape, surrounding host state, or an undeclared operation field. The shared Diagnostic ID therefore does not need profile-specific clones.

W002-HELP-002

Three-voice parity

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The Help Engine must support the three established Data Sculptor help voices. All three renderings must preserve the same diagnostic truth. Voice selection may change wording, sentence structure, degree of technical detail, and explanatory style.

F-24 session default and persistence: Technical is the canonical Help voice at the start of every new browser application instance. The analyst may select Casual or Office Speak during that instance, but WASM-002 retains the selected voice only in volatile runtime state and does not persist the preference in browser-private storage. A new application instance therefore returns to Technical. This default does not alter the F-17 rule that a missing diagnostic-specific catalog entry visibly falls back to Generic Technical Help.

W002-HELP-002.1

Voice selection must not change diagnostic identity.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-002.2

Voice selection must not change severity.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-002.3

Voice selection must not change counts or evidence.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-002.4

Voice selection must not change whether execution continues or refuses.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-002.5

Voice selection must not change safe/unsafe action boundaries.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-002.6

Voice selection must not change provenance.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-002.7

Voice selection must not change the meaning of the recommended next step.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Tests must assert parity on the canonical event and structured facts, not brittle equality of prose.

W002-HELP-002.8

One validated Help message catalog is the source of truth for all three voices

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The Help layer resolves a canonical diagnostic ID through one validated catalog that associates an authored ID with Casual, Office Speak, and Technical templates. The human-maintained development source is exactly help_messages.json, encoded as UTF-8 without BOM.

help_messages.json is a Data Sculptor product/build resource, not a Suitcase artifact. It must not use the __DS__ governed artifact namespace, consume a semantic artifact-class token, or be copied into an analyst's Suitcase merely because Data Sculptor runs. Run-specific structured facts remain authoritative in the canonical diagnostic event and are supplied separately to the selected template. The three authored voices must not be maintained as unrelated message stores.

F-17 coverage fallback: absence of an authored catalog entry for an otherwise complete registered diagnostic is permitted at run time and does not make the diagnostic incomplete. Data Sculptor must instead render the deterministic Generic Technical Help view defined by W002-HELP-002.9. The fallback consumes only the canonical event semantic core and its emitted governed facts; it is not a second message catalog and does not manufacture replacement diagnostic facts.

W002-HELP-002.9

WASM-002 may use mechanically generated placeholder voice text to prove Help wiring

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

WASM-002 acceptance does not require the complete production Help corpus. Authored catalog entries may use unmistakable placeholder strings, and placeholder entries may be generated mechanically from the validated diagnostics.json registry; no production prose authorship is required.

Deterministic Generic Technical Help fallback. When a complete registered canonical diagnostic has no matching entry in help_messages.json, all selected Help voices fall back visibly to one Generic Technical rendering. The rendering must show, in this exact conceptual order, the diagnostic ID, severity, phase, behavior, next-action token, and then every emitted governed fact ordered by ascending UTF-8 byte order of fact key. It must state that no diagnostic-specific authored explanation is available. It must not infer cause beyond the diagnostic, invent remediation, default missing facts, inspect undeclared external state, or substitute prose for governed fact values.

The Generic Technical fallback preserves the original diagnostic unchanged. Catalog incompleteness is therefore distinct from diagnostic incompleteness: a valid event can always be rendered generically, while inability to satisfy the event's own required_facts contract suppresses that intended event and produces DS-HLP-001 under W002-HELP-001.4 and W002-HELP-001.8.

Acceptance must prove correct diagnostic-ID lookup, selected-voice resolution, structured-fact interpolation where a template exists, voice switching, deterministic Generic Technical fallback for a deliberately absent catalog entry, and semantic parity across authored voices. Final authored Help wording, examples, editorial polishing, and production-corpus quality remain deferred to a later Help-content milestone.

W002-HELP-002.10

help_messages.json has one deterministic WASM-002 source schema

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The top-level JSON object has exactly two fields: catalog_version and messages. catalog_version is the string "1". messages is an array written in ascending UTF-8 byte order of diagnostic_id.

Each message entry has exactly four fields: diagnostic_id, casual, office_speak, and technical. diagnostic_id must satisfy the canonical DS-<DOMAIN>-<NNN> grammar and must be unique in the catalog. Each voice field is a JSON string.

A voice string may contain zero or more structured-fact placeholders using the exact form {fact_name}. Each catalog diagnostic_id must exist in the validated diagnostics.json registry, and each referenced placeholder must be declared in that diagnostic's required_facts or optional_facts. Duplicate IDs, missing voice fields, null voice values, malformed JSON, noncanonical or unregistered diagnostic IDs, or undeclared fact placeholders make catalog validation fail.

The catalog is intentionally allowed to be non-exhaustive. A registered diagnostic with no message entry is rendered through the deterministic Generic Technical fallback in W002-HELP-002.9. Therefore a missing catalog entry for a registered diagnostic is not a build-validation failure and must not cause the engine to synthesize an authored entry or suppress the diagnostic.

WASM-002 therefore does not require one global exhaustive fact-name table in the PRD. Fact-key authority is per diagnostic: the validated registry declares which fact names are legal for each stable diagnostic meaning.

{
  "catalog_version": "1",
  "messages": [
    {
      "diagnostic_id": "DS-ENC-001",
      "casual": "[CASUAL PLACEHOLDER] {source_filename}",
      "office_speak": "[OFFICE PLACEHOLDER] {source_filename}",
      "technical": "[TECHNICAL PLACEHOLDER] {source_filename} {first_invalid_byte_offset} {stop_reason}"
    }
  ]
}

Later Help-content revisions may extend or version this schema only through an explicit PRD revision.

F-07 placeholder mapping: Help for the strict UTF-8 refusal may render {first_invalid_byte_offset} and {stop_reason} because those exact fact names are declared by the canonical DS-ENC-001 diagnostic registry entry. The older generic {byte_offset} placeholder is not valid for DS-ENC-001.

P2-03 Help rendering duty: Help for the monotonic-UTC refusal must identify the exact blocking predecessor MAP and show both predecessor UTC and truthful observed host UTC. It must distinguish an incorrect host clock from a genuinely future-dated governed MAP and may explain the approved analyst-owned choices: correct the clock, wait/rerun after truthful time advances, or deliberately move the exact future-dated current MAP out of the active Suitcase root with the warning that an older snapshot/registry may become current and that restoring the moved MAP may restore its authority.

W002-HELP-002.11

The validated Help catalog is embedded into the released HTML build and supplied to the shared core

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Before a WASM-002 browser build is accepted, the build must parse and validate help_messages.json, then serialize the validated catalog directly into the Data Sculptor HTML itself as one non-executable application/json payload with the exact element ID ds-help-catalog.

The embedded JSON must be HTML-safe so catalog text cannot terminate the containing script element; at minimum, literal less-than characters in JSON string content must be escaped during embedding. At runtime, the browser host obtains this embedded payload and supplies the validated catalog to the shared Rust/WASM Help core. Browser JavaScript must not implement a competing template-selection, fact-interpolation, fallback, escaping, or HLP-semantic engine. The browser host must not fetch a Help catalog from the network, the filesystem, the Suitcase, or an adjacent deployment file.

Missing or malformed embedded catalog JSON, or a build whose embedded catalog does not correspond to the validated build input, is a build-validation failure. The released HTML therefore remains one offline portable front door for the browser Help catalog. A later native host may supply the same governed catalog semantics to the same shared core from its own build-bundled resource; host packaging may differ, but Help semantics must not fork.

W002-HELP-003

Message and report outputs

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The Help Engine must support both live and durable help surfaces.

W002-HELP-003.1

The Help Engine must support a concise human-facing message suitable for the live browser surface.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The concise message is rendered in the dedicated browser Help / Diagnostic Surface when that surface is present; it is not required to be a modal or transient notification.

W002-HELP-003.2

The Help Engine must support a durable HTML Help report using the canonical built-in Data Sculptor presentation suitable for saving with the Work Order, receipt, and output artifacts.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A concise Help message for an individual diagnostic and any durable Help Report that includes that diagnostic must resolve from the same canonical diagnostic event. A durable Help Report request may cover one active governed diagnostic, including a non-run diagnostic, or one governed run containing one or more canonical diagnostic events. Exactly one HLP is published for each explicit Help Report request.

W002-HELP-004

HTML Help report content

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A saved Help report must be able to include the following elements when relevant.

W002-HELP-004.1

Product and brand identity.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-004.2

Plain-language summary.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-004.3

Stable diagnostic ID.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-004.4

What Data Sculptor observed.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-004.5

Evidence and structured facts.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-004.6

What the user can safely do next.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-004.7

Source/Work-Order context is governed by the HLP disclosure allowlist.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The report may include only source and Work Order context permitted by W002-HELP-010. Durable HLP disclosure is intentionally stricter than transient local Help because the HLP is a portable support-handoff artifact.

A relevant governed alias or source header may enter the HLP only under the necessity and disclosure rules in W002-HELP-010. Source-header text is eligible only when Data Sculptor has structurally established an actual CSV header record under the governed parser. Record position alone does not make text a header. When no valid header record has been established, including the headerless-source refusal case, the HLP must use structural evidence such as the 1-based column ordinal, diagnostic condition/location, or an applicable operational fallback name and must not substitute field data from the first data row.

Absolute local paths, entire Work Orders, Work Order comments, source rows/values, unrelated headers/aliases/columns, and unrelated Suitcase contents are not automatically eligible merely because they are available to the running application.

W002-HELP-004.8

Report-generation metadata preserves HLP identity and lineage.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The report must carry its own governed HLP filename and generation UTC together with the diagnostic identity and applicable originating execution lineage. The exact HLP provenance contract is governed by W002-HELP-009.

W002-HELP-004.9

Selected Help voice and its human-facing explanation.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-004.10

A clearly labelled structured-facts block derived from the canonical diagnostic event.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-HELP-004.11

Four canonical Boolean facts describe the WASM-002 execution boundary.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

When the governed diagnostic context can determine the execution boundary, the canonical fact names are exactly:

  • source_modified_by_data_sculptor
  • materialization_started
  • analytical_outputs_published
  • store_state_committed

When one of these facts has an established Boolean value, the JSON/structured value is the native Boolean true or false, never the strings "TRUE" or "FALSE".

source_modified_by_data_sculptor states only whether Data Sculptor modified the analyst-owned source in place; it must not imply knowledge that no external process or analyst changed the source between sessions.

materialization_started records whether the governed analytical materialization phase began.

analytical_outputs_published records whether governed analytical outputs were successfully published for user use; transient SCR candidates or abandoned/uncommitted debris do not make this fact true.

store_state_committed records whether the successor Store MAP commit point was crossed.

If a present boundary fact must express governed absence rather than an established Boolean, its JSON/structured value is the exact applicable shared absence-state string "NONE", "NOT_RUN", "NOT_AVAILABLE", or "NOT_APPLICABLE". JSON null is not a valid encoding for these four boundary facts because it would discard the reason for absence. A boundary fact that is optional for a particular diagnostic may instead be omitted under W002-HELP-001.4; that omission carries no absence-state meaning.

A missing, omitted, unavailable, or not-run fact must never be interpreted as false. If one of these facts is declared required for an intended diagnostic and the required value cannot be produced, it must not be silently defaulted; the intended diagnostic is suppressed and the fail-safe DS-HLP-001 contract in W002-HELP-001.4/W002-HELP-001.8 applies.

W002-HELP-004.12

Governed Work Order lineage sufficient to establish user intent.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Included lineage must obey the disclosure boundary defined for Help reports and must not automatically expand into source-data disclosure.

W002-HELP-005

Deterministic rendering uses a closed governed input set

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Given the same canonical diagnostic event or ordered set of events, selected voice, PRETTY rules, validated Help catalog, and built-in presentation version, Help rendering must be deterministic except for explicitly permitted event/report-specific fields.

The Help renderer may consume only the canonical diagnostic fields and fact keys declared by the applicable diagnostic registry entries plus fields explicitly defined by the applicable HLP provenance schema. It must not inspect or interpolate an open-ended host-state bag, undeclared browser state, unrelated Suitcase contents, or another value merely because it is available at runtime.

A future configurable Brand Manifest may add another governed presentation input, but it is not part of the WASM-002 rendering contract.

W002-HELP-006

Host parity uses one shared Help semantic core

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The Help Engine must be designed for use by the browser host and the later native CLI host without changing diagnostic semantics. The shared Rust core owns diagnostic-to-template selection, governed fact interpolation, deterministic fallback behavior, governed escaping, and durable HLP semantic serialization.

The WASM-002 browser host supplies the validated catalog embedded under W002-HELP-002.11. A later native host may supply the same governed catalog semantics from a build-bundled native resource. Host-specific presentation and packaging may differ, but they must not create a second Help semantic engine or change canonical diagnostic identity, facts, behavior, next action, voice semantics, disclosure policy, or HLP meaning.

W002-HELP-007

Help surfaces are projections, not diagnostic authority

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The live Help / Diagnostic Surface and the saved HTML Help Report must render from the canonical diagnostic event. Neither surface may independently create, reinterpret, weaken, suppress, or override governed diagnostic truth.

W002-HELP-008

HTML Help Report is a governed support-handoff artifact

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The user must be able to generate a styled, self-contained HTML Help Report from a governed diagnostic event for retention, IT/support handoff, or communication to another analyst.

The report must support two audiences in one document: a human-readable explanation using the selected Help voice and a clearly inspectable structured-facts section that preserves the technical evidence required to understand the event.

W002-HELP-008.1

The report preserves the canonical execution-boundary facts, including relevant negative facts.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

When relevant to the diagnostic, the report must render the governed values of source_modified_by_data_sculptor, materialization_started, analytical_outputs_published, and store_state_committed. These values originate from governed execution state rather than reassuring prose invented by the renderer. A missing/unavailable fact is not rendered as false.

W002-HELP-008.2

The report preserves only the Work Order lineage needed to explain the diagnostic.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The report must identify the originating WKO physical filename when one applies and may include only the minimum executable Work Order clause or clauses needed to establish the governed operation, user intent, and trigger for the diagnostic. It must not automatically embed the entire Work Order or Work Order comments. All such context remains subject to the fixed disclosure boundary in W002-HELP-010.

W002-HELP-009

WASM-002 establishes HLP identity, lineage, multiplicity, and one canonical embedded provenance payload.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A durable generated Help Report is an immutable governed HLP artifact whose physical filename is:

__DS__HLP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.html

The UTC token is the HLP's own governed generation/publication time. The report is the final self-contained HTML artifact using the canonical built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor presentation; no unstyled intermediate is the canonical HLP.

Report-request multiplicity: one explicit Help Report request publishes exactly one HLP. The request may be bound to one active governed diagnostic, including a diagnostic that is not associated with a Run, or to one governed Run containing one or more canonical diagnostic events. A Run-level report includes the governed diagnostic events selected by that request in deterministic event order. HLP generation is never an automatic one-artifact-per-diagnostic side effect.

Every HLP must expose a visible deterministic Provenance section and exactly one embedded non-executable application/json payload whose element ID is exactly ds-hlp-provenance. F-34 supersedes the earlier draft schema version "1". For schema version "2", the JSON top-level object contains exactly these ten fields:

{
  "schema_version": "2",
  "hlp_filename": "__DS__HLP__20260922T191500123Z__<uuid-v4>.html",
  "hlp_generation_utc": "20260922T191500123Z",
  "diagnostic_ids": ["DS-ENC-001", "DS-MAT-004"],
  "originating_wko_filename": "__DS__WKO__...txt",
  "originating_rcp_filename": null,
  "selected_help_voice": "technical",
  "presentation_id": "red5sorcery-data-sculptor",
  "presentation_version": "1",
  "data_sculptor_build": "<exact-build-id>"
}

hlp_generation_utc must use the canonical fixed-width millisecond UTC form YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ. diagnostic_ids is a non-empty JSON array containing one canonical diagnostic ID for each diagnostic event included in the report, in the same deterministic event order used by the report. Repeated IDs are permitted when distinct included events legitimately share one diagnostic type. selected_help_voice is exactly one of casual, office_speak, or technical, matching the Help catalog keys. For WASM-002 the built-in presentation identity is exactly red5sorcery-data-sculptor and its presentation version is exactly "1". data_sculptor_build must contain the exact running build identifier used for the tested/released build; the literal scope label WASM-002 alone is not sufficient unless it is also the exact build identifier.

originating_wko_filename and originating_rcp_filename are schema-declared nullable lineage fields. When the relationship exists and the exact physical filename is known, the value is that filename as a JSON string. When the relationship itself does not apply to this Help event/report request, the machine-readable value is JSON null. That null has one schema-defined meaning: the nullable relationship has no value, equivalent to Rust Option<T>::None and to the governed semantic state NOT_APPLICABLE. The visible Provenance section renders it as NOT APPLICABLE.

If the lineage relationship does apply but the exact filename cannot be obtained, JSON null must not be used; the field value is the exact string "NOT_AVAILABLE" and the visible Provenance section renders NOT AVAILABLE. Empty strings, invented lineage, N/A, UNKNOWN, or another substitute are forbidden. For these two lineage fields, null and "NOT_AVAILABLE" are deliberately non-interchangeable. A non-run HLP may therefore legitimately carry JSON null for both lineage fields when neither relationship applies.

This nullable-field rule is a schema-specific serialization choice, not a fifth absence state and not a generic JSON encoding rule. Other diagnostic JSON facts follow W002-HELP-001.4 and W002-HELP-004.11. The visible and machine-readable HLP provenance must express the same governed semantics even where their physical representations differ; a semantic mismatch is an HLP-generation failure and must not be silently tolerated.

The embedded JSON must be HTML-safe so provenance text cannot terminate the containing script element; at minimum literal less-than characters in JSON string content must be escaped during embedding. The provenance payload remains subject to W002-HELP-010 and must not introduce source rows, source values, absolute local paths, arbitrary Work Order content, or other context excluded by the fixed HLP disclosure policy.

WASM-002 does not automatically compute or embed a SHA-256 of the HLP, and saving an HLP must not create, refresh, or verify an LCK. The final HLP bytes remain eligible for exact-byte integrity evidence under the later explicit FINGERPRINT/LCK workflow. Configurable Brand Manifest provenance remains deferred to V1-BACKLOG / a future build.

F-14 HLP publication: the complete self-contained report is first written as the corresponding SCR candidate under W002-STOR-023.1. It must close, reopen, and validate the required visible Provenance section, exact schema-version-2 embedded JSON shape, HTML-safe serialization, self-contained presentation and visible/machine semantic parity before the class token may be renamed from SCR to HLP. A partial or semantically mismatched candidate never becomes a canonical HLP.

W002-HELP-010

Help Report disclosure uses one fixed WASM-002 allowlist.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Generating a Help Report must not silently become a data-export path. WASM-002 therefore uses one deterministic allowlist rather than collecting broad context and attempting to redact it afterward. There are no disclosure checkboxes, permissive export modes, or per-report overrides in WASM-002.

Always eligible when present and applicable: diagnostic ID; severity/classification; governed operation/phase; continue/refuse decision; safe next action; selected Help voice; HLP identity and generation UTC; relevant governed artifact filenames; and the four canonical boundary facts from W002-HELP-004.11.

Eligible only when necessary to explain the diagnostic: the exact source filename but not an absolute OS path; a relevant source column header only when Data Sculptor has structurally established an actual CSV header record; the relevant 1-based column number; a relevant governed Store/RID/COL alias only when that alias itself is necessary to explain the diagnostic, such as an alias collision, ambiguity, or governed alias mutation; byte offset, row/count, or byte-length evidence; Store/RID/COL/MAP/WKO physical filenames; and only the minimum executable Work Order clause or clauses needed to establish intent and the diagnostic trigger. If that minimum Work Order excerpt necessarily contains a governed alias, that alias is disclosed and counts as alias text included.

Headerless boundary: record position alone never establishes a source header. If the governed parser has not established a valid header record, including a headerless-source refusal, HLP generation must not treat any field from the first data row or any later data record as header text. Structural evidence such as 1-based column ordinal, governed diagnostic/location facts, or an applicable operational fallback name must be used instead.

Never included automatically: source rows; source field values or arbitrary data samples; field data mislabeled as header text; absolute local paths; unrelated source headers, aliases, or column names; the complete Work Order; Work Order comments; unrelated Suitcase contents; browser/environment internals not governed as diagnostic evidence; or raw ungoverned stack traces.

Every generated HLP must contain a visible Disclosure section stating, at minimum: Source rows included: NO; Source values included: NO; Source header text included: YES or NO; Governed alias text included: YES or NO; Absolute local paths included: NO; Work Order comments included: NO; and Work Order excerpt: RELEVANT EXECUTABLE CLAUSES ONLY. The two YES/NO declarations must truthfully reflect the actual HLP bytes. A genuine established source header does not count as a source field value; this distinction applies only after the governed parser has established the header record. The renderer must not weaken any declaration when the underlying policy has not changed.

This durable-HLP allowlist does not prohibit transient local Help from showing a relevant governed alias or a genuinely established source header when useful to explain the same canonical diagnostic event. Local presentation does not enlarge what the portable HLP may disclose.

W002-HELP-011

Help owns the cross-session source-continuity edge-case explanation

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

When an unexpected analytical result, row-alignment concern, or support question raises the possibility that an analyst-owned source changed between sessions, Data Sculptor-controlled guidance must flow through the Help Engine. Help must not imply that the engine monitored or cryptographically protected the source when it did not.

The explanation must distinguish ordinary analyst-controlled workflow from stronger optional evidence. It may ask whether the analyst edited, replaced, sorted, re-exported, synchronized, copied over, or otherwise changed the source after the Store was established.

W002-HELP-011.1

Help presents continuity evidence in explicit assurance levels

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

For a suspected cross-session source change, Help must distinguish at least these evidence levels:

  • No continuity evidence: state that cross-session byte continuity cannot be independently verified from filename/Store metadata alone.
  • INVENTORY available: use filename, exact byte length, and last-modified metadata as lightweight clues; changed metadata may indicate that the source changed, while unchanged metadata must not be presented as proof of unchanged bytes.
  • Explicit fingerprint evidence available: exact-byte SHA-256 evidence may establish whether the compared file bytes match or differ under the later governed FINGERPRINT workflow.

Help must not collapse these levels into one generic statement of certainty.

W002-HELP-011.2

WASM-002 does not impose automatic cross-session hashing or Suitcase surveillance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Ordinary WASM-002 materialization and Store inheritance must not automatically SHA-256 the source, recursively fingerprint the Suitcase, or maintain hidden whole-Suitcase surveillance merely to guard against the possibility that an analyst-owned file changed between sessions.

This is an intentional product boundary for the lone-office-analyst model. The product assumes the analyst normally controls the Suitcase, provides lightweight explicit INVENTORY evidence in WASM-002, preserves a later explicit FINGERPRINT path for stronger assurance, and relies on Help to explain unusual cross-session continuity questions proportionately.

WASM-002 must not create, refresh, or silently verify an LCK Suitcase Lock as a side effect of Work Order save, materialization, Store inheritance, INVENTORY, alias maintenance, or ordinary project use. LCK publication belongs to the explicit later-V1 FINGERPRINT workflow.

F-13 single-writer Help boundary: Help must distinguish cross-session continuity from concurrent writing. WASM-002 does not claim that two Data Sculptor tabs/windows can safely write the same Suitcase at once. User guidance must say to use one writing Data Sculptor context per Suitcase; read-only viewing is not itself a governed write. When a pre-commit guard detects that relevant governed state changed underneath an operation, Help must identify the changed authority where available and direct the analyst to refresh or reopen current state and rerun deliberately. It must not imply that Data Sculptor acquired a cross-tab lock, merged the competing work, or automatically rebased the refused transaction.

PRETTY Engine — First-Class Rendering Surface

W002-PRETTY-001

Separation of truth and presentation

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The PRETTY Engine must not decide analytical truth or reinterpret diagnostic meaning. It receives governed content and renders it into human-facing artifacts.

WASM-002 conceptual boundary: ENGINE TRUTH -> HELP / REPORT CONTENT -> PRETTY ENGINE -> BUILT-IN DATA SCULPTOR PRESENTATION -> ARTIFACT.

A future build may replace the built-in presentation source with a governed Brand Manifest without changing the analytical or diagnostic truth supplied to PRETTY.

W002-PRETTY-002

Shared renderer path

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The PRETTY Engine must provide a common rendering path for Data Sculptor artifacts that require governed human presentation, including at minimum the WASM-002 Help HTML report. WASM-002 uses the canonical built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor presentation. The architecture must permit the same path to accept a configurable Brand Manifest in a future build without changing analytical semantics.

The architecture must also permit later reuse for branded Receipt HTML, verification reports, tables, Quick Viz, and other PRETTY outputs. WASM-002 canonical run Receipts themselves remain TXT-only under W002-RCP-003.

W002-PRETTY-003

Self-contained HTML

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Durable HTML artifacts produced by PRETTY must be self-contained for ordinary viewing after generation. Self-containment requires semantic and functional portability, not pixel-identical rendering across operating systems or browsers; ordinary system-font substitution and browser rendering differences are acceptable when meaning, evidence, hierarchy, and accessibility remain intact.

W002-PRETTY-003.1

A saved artifact must not require a network connection.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-PRETTY-003.2

A saved artifact must not require an external stylesheet.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-PRETTY-003.3

A saved artifact must not require a remote font.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-PRETTY-003.4

A saved artifact must not require a separately located logo file.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-PRETTY-003.5

A saved artifact must not require external presentation resources.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Required CSS, SVG, and other built-in presentation assets needed for ordinary viewing must be embedded or otherwise resolved into the generated artifact at creation time.

Future configurable Brand Manifest inputs, when implemented, must preserve this self-contained output rule.

W002-PRETTY-004

Accessibility and inspectability

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

PRETTY HTML must remain ordinary inspectable HTML. Presentation must not obscure the text, evidence, diagnostic code, provenance, or next-step guidance. The rendered artifact must remain usable without JavaScript when JavaScript is not required for its content.

PRETTY Engine — PRETTY Tables and Contextual

Handoff The following requirements extend the first-class PRETTY rendering surface with the V1 PRETTY Table handoff model. They do not change the separation of truth and presentation established by W002-PRETTY-001.

W002-PRETTY-005

PRETTY Table renderer

DEFERRED
SCOPEV1-BACKLOGBUILD—

The PRETTY Engine must be able to render a finalized governed tabular result into a review-ready XLSX artifact without recalculating or reinterpretating analytical values.

W002-PRETTY-005.1

DEFERRED
SCOPEV1-BACKLOGBUILD—

The rendered workbook may apply governed titles, headings, widths, panes, number formats, hierarchy, notes, and other presentation details defined by the PRETTY contract and Brand Manifest.

W002-PRETTY-005.2

DEFERRED
SCOPEV1-BACKLOGBUILD—

Any value written to the primary governed result table must correspond to an already-established analytical result or an explicitly governed presentation-only representation of that result.

W002-PRETTY-006

Rich Footnote model

DEFERRED
